cards.name: Two-pass parallel test run (pytest-xdist, 6 workers, one database per worker, serial pass for race tests)
cards.what_it_is: The check's test step is split in two. Parallel pass: pytest -m 'not serial' -p xdist.plugin -n 6 --dist load, each worker with its own test database (_gw0, _gw1...). Serial pass: -m serial, one process, for 128 tests at first (two-connection race harness modules, three elapsed-time assertions, one parametrized test with random ids, one database-name test). judge_split proves the two passes partition the suite and every collected id ran exactly once; skipped/xfailed/xpassed still fail. Owner decision USER-22 (5 Nov 2026) approved the dev-only dependency after the owner asked why a check takes ten minutes on a 12-core machine.
cards.measured: Baseline 1878b2f one process: whole check 855.2 s, 1,953 tests (task.md:11; evidence/baseline-check-alone.log last lines '1953 passed in 848.26s', 'TOTAL exit=0' at 855.2 s). After, 6 workers + serial pass: 268.3 to 298.3 s over 12 full runs, mean 283.8 s, about 3.0x faster (task.md:11). Parallel pass 160-190 s for 1,844 tests, serial pass 104-105 s for 128 tests (task.md:13). Merged tree 3d87109 (1,997 tests): CLINIC_CHECK_WORKERS 0 = 746.7 s, 2 = 443.9 s, 4 = 319.6 s, 6 = 289.4-290.7 s (six runs), 8 = 281.1 s (task.md:177-185); one-process vs default 2.6x. Owner's own measurement before the work: 999 s of tests for 1,953 tests while three other checks ran (clinic-planning-brief.md:44). Board verified the merged main: 7/7 in 286 s, 1,997 tests (clinic-build/task.md:29).
cards.limits: The serial pass is 36-37 percent of wall time (104 s of about 283 s, task.md:13, :185), mostly fixed 0.6 s waits in the race harness. Eight workers gain only 3 percent over six (task.md:185). Check needs a live Postgres container. Window-to-Docker path remains (A3-10). Parallel gain was measured with the owner's PC partly idle of other checks.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: FixFlow backend pytest + Postgres could use the same shape: xdist with a per-worker database suffix, an explicit 'serial' marker for threads/timing tests, and a proof step that compares collected ids per pass so a split can never silently drop a test. The id-partition proof (judge_split) and the 'a skipped test still fails' rule transfer directly; worker count must be re-measured for FixFlow (the knee here was 6 of 24 threads).

cards.name: Worker-count and distribution-mode decisions (6 workers; load not loadfile)
cards.what_it_is: Default 6 workers (or half the logical processors if fewer, default_workers: 24 give 6, 8 give 4). --dist load chosen over loadfile because loadfile was about 3 percent faster but hung when a worker died (replacement worker never finished), whereas load counts the crash at once. Per-worker databases are created from migrations, not cloned from a template (template saves at most about 3 s of 165 s, stale-template risk).
cards.measured: Parallel pass only, loadfile, alone: 6 workers 171 s, 8 workers 169 s (task.md:32). loadfile 282-292 s against load 296-298 s whole check (task.md:38). Dying-worker demo: loadfile ran 754 s until the 600 s watchdog; load failed in 274 s (task.md:38, :65). Worker DB migrate about 13 s when six do it at once, first test at 15.6 s vs 8-10 s single (task.md:34).
cards.limits: Template-clone claim is INFERRED from the numbers, not run (task.md:34). Knee measurements were taken on a shared machine ('alone among my own runs'); the container-mode sweep later put the knee between 6 and 12 (A3-11).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Choose the distribution mode by failure behaviour as well as speed; measure the worker knee on the actual machine (here a shared DB container, not CPU, capped the gain). Do not clone from a template unless migrations dominate start-up.

cards.name: Non-durable test database settings
cards.what_it_is: The dev/test Postgres container runs with fsync=off, synchronous_commit=off, full_page_writes=off in compose.yaml only (deploy/ untouched, git diff of deploy and docker empty). An existing container needs docker compose up -d --wait db once to pick it up.
cards.measured: 316 s to 297 s on single runs, 'inside the noise' (task.md:44). One-process run with non-durable DB 746.7 s vs unmodified baseline 855.2 s, but the two figures are on different tree sizes so are not a clean comparison (task.md:185).
cards.limits: Small, unproven gain: the check is described as CPU-bound not flush-bound. No isolated A/B with matched runs.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Cheap to copy for a local Postgres test container (three flags), but expect a small gain; do not rely on it. Keep it out of any production config.

cards.name: Startup cost found by tracing: pytest tmp_path symlink (about 32 s) removed with --basetemp
cards.what_it_is: The xdist controller calls pytest base-temp creation before any worker starts; on this Windows machine os.symlink took about 32 s. Found by dumping controller tracebacks with faulthandler; fixed by passing --basetemp <fresh dir> from check.py. Same defect already worked around in tests by a scratch_dir fixture.
cards.measured: 43 s to 11.5 s on a 16-test run (task.md:36).
cards.limits: Windows-specific; cause of the slow symlink not explained.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: On the same Windows PC, FixFlow pytest runs with tmp_path would hit the same 32 s per base-temp creation: pass --basetemp or avoid tmp_path. Generally: profile the harness start-up with faulthandler before blaming the tests.

cards.name: Baseline profile: no hot spot, cost is 1,953 small tests
cards.what_it_is: A --durations=40 run on the unmodified suite showed the slowest test 16 s and the 40 slowest summing to about 190 s of 843 s, so speed could only come from parallelism, not from fixing a few slow tests.
cards.measured: Pytest alone 843.3 s (evidence/baseline-pytest-durations.log last lines), whole check 855.2 s; first test finishes at about 14.2 s (collection plus DB setup) in the durations log head; static steps total about 5 s: ruff lint 0.3, ruff format 0.3, mypy 2.1, Django checks 0.7, migrations 0.8, probe 0.7 (task.md:12).
cards.limits: One profile on one day.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Run --durations first; if the tail is flat, go straight to parallelism rather than optimising individual tests.

cards.name: Machine-wide test lock (file lock outside checkouts, in the git common directory) and its evolution
cards.what_it_is: Root's request after two unclean PC shutdowns (5 and 6 Nov) with several worktrees running full checks. check.py takes an OS file lock (msvcrt.locking / fcntl.flock) around the test step only. First version: per-user dir %LOCALAPPDATA%\clinic-check; FC-03 moved it to <git common dir>/clinic-check/check.lock so every worktree resolves to the same file, no env override; FC-16 refuses when the checkout is not the top of its own git checkout. A waiting check prints the holder (worktree, pid, start time) at once and then each minute; wait bounded to 2700 s (45 min) via CLINIC_CHECK_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS; never runs unlocked silently; CLINIC_CHECK_NO_LOCK=1 skips it and is reported. A killed holder releases it (no stale-lock logic). Until every live worktree merged the follow-up, a cooperative directory lock clinic-full-check.lock in the temp folder was also used; retired 6 Nov (USER-23).
cards.measured: Wait bound 2700 s is a chosen figure, not measured (task.md:169). Observed waits: 385 s for the single slot on the merged main (clinic-build/task.md:732).
cards.limits: Does not exclude another clone, another user account or a check run with NO_LOCK (task.md:213 FC-03 row, :245). Not fair: a newcomer can take the slot a long waiter was about to get (FS-06, task.md:351). Lock generations before 83ff8dd do not interact with later ones (task.md:263, :348). Mitigates the shutdowns, root cause never diagnosed.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A git-common-dir OS file lock is a portable way to serialise heavy jobs across every worktree of one repository on one PC with automatic release on kill; stdlib only. Print the holder so a waiting session knows who to blame; bound the wait. FixFlow should add it before running parallel Claude sessions each doing a full check.

cards.name: Check slots: two concurrent checks (TEST_SLOTS = 2) plus per-checkout lock
cards.what_it_is: FC-19: the lock became a set of slots (slot 0 = old check.lock, slot i = check.lock.i, each with a holder file); a check takes any free slot and waits only if all are taken; the count is the constant TEST_SLOTS = 2 in check.py, no env override. FS-02: a CheckoutLock (file named by hash of the real checkout path) refuses a second check of the same checkout at once because two would share and could drop each other's test databases; taken even with CLINIC_CHECK_NO_LOCK. Test databases are named test_<name>_<hash of checkout path>_gw<N> (FC-04), name length counted in bytes with room for _gw999 (FC-11).
cards.measured: Five pairs of full checks started together (task.md:298-307, evidence/slot-pairs/summary.txt): pair 1 two checks of mine, 435.1 and 435.6 s, no wait; pairs 2-5 one of mine waited 409, 364, 469, 337 s behind a foreign check, whole 831.3, 787.0, 854.8, 692.2 s. Single references taken right after: 389.4 and 417.6 s (task.md:308), against 275-290 s on the quiet machine (task.md:313). Cost of a second check 4 to 12 percent per check, throughput about 1.8 to 1.9x vs loaded single, 1.29x vs quiet (task.md:314). Machine during pairs: cpu mean 41-58 percent, free memory min 8.5, 3.3, 2.3, 2.5, 5.6 GB of 31 (slot-pairs/summary.txt). Second set on final code 8fff426 (task.md:362-367): wholes 476.2, 791.5, 622.0, 1,072.9, 1,110.5, 734.0 s, waits 0, 338, 0, 551, 726, 221 s; free memory min 0.8, 0.0, 3.4 GB (fs-pairs/summary.txt).
cards.limits: Only pair 1 is two of the owner's own checks; the rest are mixed with other sessions' checks so they measure waits, not isolated overlap (task.md:312). Machine never idle, so no clean baseline. Waiting is unfair (FS-06). Three slots rejected for memory reasons (task.md:318).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A slot count (not a boolean mutex) with a printed holder list and a per-checkout lock is the useful pattern when several Claude sessions each run the gate. Pick the slot count from measured memory, not CPU. The pairs/sampler harness (a once-a-second CPU and free-memory CSV beside each run) is a reusable measurement method.

cards.name: Memory headroom guard on the second slot (8 GiB)
cards.what_it_is: FS-08: MachineLock(second_slot_free_gb, free_memory) offers slot 1 only while at least 8.0 GiB of physical memory is available, re-read at every poll; otherwise a check waits for the first slot as if there were one. Reads GlobalMemoryStatusEx via ctypes on Windows (ullAvailPhys = free plus standby), MemAvailable in /proc/meminfo elsewhere; unreadable = second slot closed. SECOND_SLOT_FREE_GB = 8.0 constant in check.py, no env override; summary prints the rule applied and the free memory seen. Chosen in response to the unclean shutdowns and the pairs showing free memory fell to 0.0-0.8 GB.
cards.measured: Three full checks on 164528e (task.md:400-403): solo run 1 whole 1,063.4 s of which 647 s waited, parallel 249.8, serial 157.9, 4.0 GiB free; solo run 2 405.5 s, wait 3, 246.6/148.6, 3.9 GiB; run 3 A 639.7 s wait 256, B 1,020.4 s wait 614. About 980 one-second samples: 8 GiB was never available; free memory 2.1-4.7 GiB (mean 3.5) run 1, 2.4-4.6 (3.4) run 2, 3.9-6.2 (5.2) run 3; cpu mean 24-36 percent, peak 82 (task.md:405). The 8 GiB is 'a safety margin, not a measured requirement' (task.md:407). Check's own memory footprint was not measured (task.md:407).
cards.limits: The gate reads memory only at admission: a second check arriving while the first is still ramping its workers sees memory as free (task.md:394). Older checkouts run two slots without the gate. No measurement of two overlapping checks under the gate exists, because 8 GiB was never free, so in practice the gate collapses to one slot and queueing returns (waits 256 to 647 s). That is the direct link to B07. Inside a Linux container MemAvailable would be the host's.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Reading available memory before admitting a heavy job is a small stdlib guard that FixFlow can reuse for its own check or for starting sessions/containers. But the owner should measure per-check footprint first; the 8 GiB constant was a guess and it effectively serialises checks when idle sessions and containers hold memory (B08). A guard on idle-session count or container count may matter more than a threshold on free RAM.

cards.name: Stall watchdog, heartbeat and process-tree guard (the 600 s figure and the one observed hang)
cards.what_it_is: pytest_outcomes plugin touches a heartbeat file on every collection and test event; no event for CLINIC_CHECK_STALL_SECONDS (default 600) kills the pass tree and fails with 'no test made progress for Ns'. FC-02: on Windows every pytest is created suspended, assigned to a job object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, then resumed, so the whole tree dies when the check dies by any means; every exit path of the wait kills the tree; SIGTERM/SIGHUP/Ctrl-Break turn into SystemExit. FC-13: job terminated and closed after each pass. POSIX gets a new session and PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, with documented gaps (grandchildren, macOS).
cards.measured: Demo D: a test sleeping an hour with the stall limit at 60 s was killed and the check failed with the message (task.md:66). THE 600-SECOND HANG (B09): on bc572f6, native 6 workers, run m1, the parallel pass stalled at about 96 percent of tests, 'no test made progress for 600s', watchdog killed it after 961 s, whole check 1,116.0 s; the serial pass passed (155 s); the rerun m2 passed 7/7 in 475.5 s with parallel 324.5 s (linux-test-runner/task.md:218-219). Host free memory was under 1 GB at the time; the log shows no failure, only the stall; the hung test is not identified because the heartbeat reports no test id; not reproduced (linux-test-runner/task.md:221). Unguarded control run left child and grandchild alive, guarded run killed both (task.md:212).
cards.limits: The hang's cause is unknown and the watchdog cannot name the hung test. A hung pass costs the whole 600 s before it is killed (task.md:104), so one hang costs about 10 minutes. A single healthy test longer than 600 s would also be killed. POSIX grandchildren not covered (FC-17). The hung-test watchdog inside the Linux container was only shown on a planted sleep test (linux-test-runner/task.md:225), not on a real hang.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A progress heartbeat plus a stall deadline turns a silent hang into a fail-fast with a message; the Windows job-object kill-on-close is the right way to stop orphan pytest/browser processes when a session dies. Improvement not done here: record the last started test id in the heartbeat so a hang is attributable, and lower the stall limit well under 600 s for a suite whose longest test is 16 s.

cards.name: What stayed slow: Windows-to-Docker socket path, the 0.6 s race-harness serial pass, and a memory-bound machine
cards.what_it_is: Root's measurements on 6 Nov for the dropped FC-20: during one check's parallel pass the whole machine was 42 percent of 24 logical processors, the six Python workers together 2.45 cores (each busy about 40 percent of the time), the Docker/WSL VM 2.7 cores of which Postgres about 1.0, com.docker.backend (published-port forwarder) 0.7 cores. A trivial query from Windows via the published port took 0.63 ms against about 0.13 ms inside the container. Workers are waiting on the path, not on CPU. Eight workers gained 3 percent over six. FC-20 (a database-path fix) was dropped in favour of a Linux container beside the database (USER-23).
cards.measured: 0.63 ms vs 0.13 ms per trivial query; 42 percent of 24 processors; 2.45 cores of Python workers; Docker VM 2.7 cores; forwarder 0.7 cores; free memory 10.8 of 31 GB at that moment (task.md:322). Brief: 0.4 of 24 processors busy while a check waited behind a VM drill (clinic-planning-brief.md:44). Serial pass about 104-105 s on a quiet native machine, 118-165 s under load (task.md:13, :314, :362-367).
cards.limits: Cause attribution to the port path is INFERRED, not isolated by an A/B (the container run is the closest A/B, A3-11). The serial pass (about 36-40 percent of wall time) was never split or sped up; its safety margin under load was reasoned about, not measured. FS-01 later removed its time dependence for correctness but not its cost.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Before adding workers, check whether workers are idle waiting on a network hop; on the same Windows+Docker PC, FixFlow's pytest against a published-port Postgres will pay the same 0.5 ms per query. Running tests beside the database (container or WSL) is the lever, not CPU count.

cards.name: Linux test container beside the database (CLINIC_CHECK_MODE=container) as a faster alternative path
cards.what_it_is: USER-23 (6 Nov): the owner chose 'run the test in a linux container next to the database'. container_mode.py runs all seven steps in a Debian 12 / Python 3.13 image on the compose network of the checkout's database container against a verified copy of the working tree (git ls-files based, nested worktrees excluded); the host takes the machine-wide lock and slot first and holds it for the whole run; failures never fall back to native; the container dies 0.6 s after the host is killed. Default 12 workers or half Docker's processors. Native Windows mode stays and is still the gate.
cards.measured: Final head df66fc8, 2,246 tests (linux-test-runner/task.md:9-16): container 12 workers whole 247.0, 215.6, 227.7 s (mean 230.1), parallel mean 117.9, serial mean 94.0; native 6 workers on the same tree 367.2 s (236.1 parallel, 126.5 serial); earlier native 346.8, 336.8. About 1.5x faster whole, parallel 1.9x. Start-up 6-7 s, with collection 16 s (:18); mypy 9.7 s vs 1.4 s because of a cold cache (:94). Worker sweep in container mode (:83-92): 6 workers 244.6 s, 9 workers 245.4, 12 workers 207.3-247.0, 16 workers 203.7-234.8; knee between 6 and 12 with about 15 s noise. Two container checks at once: 266.4 and 267.0 s at 12 workers, 285.9 and 283.0 s at 6 (:98). Heavily loaded day on bc572f6: container 331.3, 360.1, 318.8 s versus native 475.5 s (:213-219). Memory low point in container runs 4.7-5.1 GB, native 5.0 GB (:94 area). All three container runs at bc572f6 and three at df66fc8 green.
cards.limits: Status is built and verified but the root decides which mode is the gate (task.md:19); wave board still describes the Windows check as the gate. Container-mode is optional so B06 and B18 are only mitigated. The 12-worker gain over 6 is 'defensible but not established' (:92). The serial pass (about 92 s) is 40 percent of the container check and was not split. A planted hung test was run in the container only with a short stall limit, not a real hang. Container memory not sampled.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Directly transferable: run FixFlow's backend pytest inside a Linux container on the Postgres container's network, and also get Linux parity for free (production is Linux). The same host-side lock, tree copy by git ls-files, and image-tag-from-install-inputs checks apply. Measure container memory and use the same worker sweep.

cards.name: Gate integrity proofs: every test runs exactly once, nothing weaker, demos of failure paths
cards.what_it_is: The faster gate had to be no weaker than the one it replaced. judge_tests per pass, judge_split (parallel ids equal serial's left-out ids, disjoint), judge_workers (each worker's final status, found by an Opus review as P1), combine totals; summary lines unchanged. Four failure demos run on full checks: failing/skipped/erroring/xfail/xpass in parallel pass, the same in serial pass, a worker killed by os._exit(7), a one-hour sleep with 60 s stall. Collected ids compared to the baseline (1,953 baseline ids, 0 missing, 0 in both passes; later merged-tree comparisons 1,997 and 2,013). Six Opus reviews recorded; the root's gate verified independently with a plain collect-only list and its own demonstration run (collected=2003 finished=2003 passed=1997 failed=2 errors=2 skipped=1 xfailed=1 CHECK FAILED).
cards.measured: Baseline 1,953 ids vs 1,972 (parallel 1,844 + serial 128, none in both, 19 added) (task.md:93); merged 1,997 = 1,869 + 128 (task.md:187); FC round 2,013 = 1,885 + 128 (task.md:239). Round 6 found a P1 of the session's own: the commit failed the check's own mypy step with five errors because ruff and tests were run but not mypy before committing (task.md:394).
cards.limits: Verification is model-written and model-reviewed (Opus reviewers briefed to refute); no human reviewer. Each review round still found new P2s in the previous round's fixes (see A3-13), which is B01 in miniature.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The id-partition proof and the 'demo each failure kind on a real full run' habit transfer. So does a root re-verification that runs its own independent collect-only list instead of trusting the session's report (the board did this, clinic-build/task.md:701).

cards.name: Review rounds on the faster check: fixes created new defects (a B01 case study)
cards.what_it_is: One session produced eleven commits, then needed follow-up rounds FC-01..09, FC-10..18, FC-19, FS-01..07 and FS-08/09/KG-02/04, each triggered by the root's or an Opus reviewer's finding on the previous round. Examples: the connection-retry delay (0.05 s x attempt, up to 0.75 s) was longer than the race harness's 0.6 s window and could make a race look blocked (FC-01, found one round after it was written); a sequence-reset fixture was written, reviewed, found pointless (premise false, UUID primary keys) and reverted; the first full check after adding the checkout lock failed on the session's own test that called the real lock (task.md:354); the lock-slot code let a slow second call pass as 'blocked' (FS-01); the memory-gate commit failed mypy.
cards.measured: none (counts only): FC-01 to FC-18 plus FC-19, FS-01 to FS-09 across six Opus review records (evidence/review-opus-round1..6.md); the gate round after merge opened nine P2/P3 items FC-01 to FC-09 on a change that had already passed gate (clinic-build/task.md:703-714).
cards.limits: The faster check ended closed, with FS-06 (unfair waiting) and the gate-reads-memory-only-at-admission P2 recorded, not fixed.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The recurring shape: a change that is correct for the measured case gets a second-order defect from the very safety margin it adds (a retry delay longer than the observation window; a lock that blocks its own test). A cheap pre-commit run of every step the gate runs (including mypy) would have caught the P1; make the full local gate run before any commit by the author.

cards.name: Random-tag flaky tests surfaced by parallel runs and fixed (random_tag, without_identifiers, layout guard)
cards.what_it_is: Parallel runs exposed three pre-existing chance failures (test data with uuid4().hex[:6] tags containing digit strings such as '40' that a test asserts absent). FC-09 added random_tag() (letters only), without_identifiers() (strips UUIDs, hex digests, CSRF value), converted 33 uses in 21 files plus about 20 assertions, and a layout test (test_no_hex_tags.py) that fails if the old forms return (extended in FC-15). The gate's reliability, not its speed.
cards.measured: 2 of 12 final runs failed on the first test (task.md:79); about 3 failures in about 40 full runs (task.md:189); overall 10 of 12 green in the final set; after the fix, four consecutive green default runs b1 to b4 (283.4, 315.0, 307.3, 304.7 s) (task.md:231-234) and three c1-c3 (281.4, 278.4, 275.1 s) (task.md:277-279).
cards.limits: Sample is small; FC-18 (removing the root's masking NOT_FIGURES) deliberately waited and was not done (task.md:271); random values elsewhere may recur.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Speed work finds flakiness: budget for it. A static guard test that forbids random hex in test data is a cheap permanent fix; FixFlow's Hypothesis/uuid-based fixtures should be audited the same way before parallelising.

cards.name: Race harness decides 'blocked' from the database, not from time (FS-01, KG-02)
cards.what_it_is: Under two concurrent checks a slow second call looked 'blocked' after a 0.6 s join, so a race test could pass with a broken lock. blocked_by_a_lock(second, first) in clinic.operations.testing now requires the second thread alive and a session of the current database waiting for a lock (pg_stat_activity.wait_event_type = 'Lock'), polled up to 15 s, with the first call's backend among pg_blocking_pids; one query (lock_waits) feeds hold_then_race, pause_then_race and race_and_see.
cards.measured: All 143 serial tests pass with the harness, 184 s (task.md:345); later 159 passed, 2,262 deselected, 189 s (task.md:392). 59 'blocked' assertions in 13 test files migrated, 4 'not blocked' (task.md:345).
cards.limits: Does not show which lock; a removed lock can still read as blocked if the second call queues on another lock the first holds (task.md:346). The serial pass cost was not reduced.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Replace sleep-and-check concurrency assertions with a database-observed wait; this makes timing tests safe to run beside other load, which is the precondition for ever shrinking the serial pass.

cards.name: Loopback socket refusal retry (No buffer space available, 10055)
cards.what_it_is: Two of the first 22 full runs failed in the serial race pass with psycopg 'No buffer space available (0x00002747/10055)' on the loopback connect. TIME_WAIT samples peaked at 352 sockets for the DB port, so ephemeral-port exhaustion was ruled out; cause not identified. connect_retry.py retries only that error, flat 0.02 s delay up to five times; any retry in the serial pass fails the step; a retry in the parallel pass is reported only.
cards.measured: Time-wait samples: all=621 db55450=289 falling to 190 across the run (evidence/final-runs/time-wait-samples-during-run-6.log); no further 10055 failure in 17 full runs after the retry (task.md:46).
cards.limits: Root cause not identified (INFERRED transient machine pressure); also reported near the memory-pressure suspected in B05. The same Windows-networking symptom class may link to the unexplained hang (A3-09) but nothing recorded ties them.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: If FixFlow tests open many loopback connections from parallel workers on this PC, expect the same refusal; a narrow, bounded retry that cannot alter test observation is the precedent.

cards.name: Queueing behaviour and measured waits for the test lock
cards.what_it_is: Collected waits for a test-lock slot from the records: waits caused by other sessions' checks holding the slots, with the holder named in the printed message (worktree names, process id, start time). Single slot: 385 s (clinic-build gate). Two slots with the 8 GiB gate: waits 647, 3, 256, 614 s. Pairs: 337-469 s, then 221-726 s.
cards.measured: Waits (s): 385 single-slot (clinic-build/task.md:732); 409, 364, 469, 337 (task.md:301-307); 338, 551, 726, 221 (task.md:363-367); 647, 3, 256, 614 (task.md:400-403); 443 and 169 in the container/native runs (linux-test-runner/task.md:217,219). Largest single recorded wait here is 726 s; the owner's B07 figure of up to 34 minutes (2,040 s) is NOT in any file I read; the wait cap is 2700 s (task.md:169).
cards.limits: Waits are determined by who else runs; the guard keeps them from shrinking while memory is under 8 GiB (A3-08). No fairness (FS-06). Waiting sessions sit idle holding context and sometimes their own container, which links to B08/B15.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Queueing is the real cost of a shared gate: a check that costs about 5 minutes alone costs 10-18 minutes with two to four sessions. FixFlow should decide up front whether to run the gate once per merge (orchestrator) rather than per slice session, or to shard it.

cards.name: Recorded operational lessons for other sessions (how work was handed over)
cards.what_it_is: The faster-check record proposes exact old/new text for the shared documents (command catalogue, development guide, version manifest, conventions) because slice sessions cannot edit shared documents; the root applies them in the gate commit. A hand-over note faster-check-handover.md in a shared notes folder tells other sessions what changes (existing containers need docker compose up -d --wait db once; check takes about five minutes; leftover test_<name>_gw<N> databases are harmless; new *_races.py modules must be marked serial). Rules created: a test that asserts elapsed time or holds a transaction open is marked serial; random labels via random_tag; race tests use the harness helpers; tests that call the lock code pass a scratch lock directory.
cards.measured: none
cards.limits: Single-writer shared documents are the cause of B13: this mechanism moves the editing to the orchestrator, it does not remove it. The record is about 416 lines, itself token-heavy for any session that must read it.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Writing the shared-doc change as exact old/new text lets the orchestrator apply it by script without re-reading the whole slice. FixFlow could keep such patches as machine-appliable files rather than prose in a 400-line record.

result.notes:
Plain answer to the owner's recollection: nothing in lane A3 is a SQLite graph library or a token-saving recall mechanism. The only 'self-evolving' ingredients here are the check's self-proofs (collected-id partition, judge_* functions, layout tests that police their own conventions) and the memory-aware lock; those are verification and resource mechanisms, not recall. What the owner may be remembering lives in another lane, not this one.

Key facts for the harness: (1) speed went from 855 s to about 275-290 s (3.0x) native and about 230 s in container mode (1.5x more, on one day), with a serial pass of 92-105 s that was never reduced and now dominates; (2) the 'queue behind each other' (B07) is dominated by the shared slots and the 8 GiB memory gate that was never satisfied in about 980 samples, so in practice the gate admits one check at a time; waits recorded are 169 to 726 s; (3) the single 600 s hang (B09) is a native-mode stall at about 96 percent with under 1 GB free memory and cost 961 s of parallel pass, unexplained and not reproduced; (4) the speedup work itself needed about six review rounds, each finding defects in the previous round's fixes (B01) and the session's own P1 (mypy failure) shows why a full local gate before commit matters; (5) the lock, slot and memory constants are literals in check.py with no env overrides by deliberate design, so nothing adapts to current load. Line numbers for faster-check/task.md are as printed by the Read tool; those for linux-test-runner/task.md come from sed -n (line numbers in sed output); within-file offsets for the 'Container sweep' rows are approximate to the nearest few lines.

result.lane: A4: Linux test runner, staging rig, drills, real-host gap (clinic repo, docs/tasks/{linux-test-runner,staging-rig,s11-operations,s12-pilot,query-followup}, deploy/, docker/tests, compose.yaml)

cards.name: Container mode of the check: all seven steps in a Linux container beside the database
cards.what_it_is: CLINIC_CHECK_MODE=container runs scripts/check.py's seven steps (ruff, format, mypy, Django checks, migrations, DB probe, pytest in a parallel pass plus a serial pass) inside a Debian 12 / Python 3.13.18 container on the compose network of the checkout's Postgres container (db:5432, no published port). The host copies the working tree (git ls-files tracked+untracked-not-ignored) as a tar over stdin, hashes it with a SHA-256 manifest, and bootstrap.py verifies file by file before running. The image is built once (clinic-tests:<hash of Dockerfile, uv.lock, pyproject install part>), never built or pulled by a check, and never falls back to native. Same run_steps/judge code as native, so the faster-check guarantees (every test exactly once, skips/xfails fail) are shared code, not copies.
where: compose.yaml (service tests, profile tests, tests-internal network)
cards.measured: Final head df66fc8, 2,246 tests: container mean 230.1 s whole (parallel 117.9, serial 94.0) vs native 6 workers 367.2 s (parallel 236.1, serial 126.5) (task.md:9-16); 'about 1.5 times faster as a whole (230 s against 350 s, 34 percent less)', parallel pass 1.9x, serial 1.3x (task.md:18). Container start-up 6-7 s, with collection 16 s; 2,246 tests collected in 4.7 s (task.md:94). Image: 2.28 GB, cold build 6 min 28 s, rebuild 3-14 s when only last layers change (task.md:35). Archive of 1,889 files / 64 MB takes 2.1 s; main checkout 2,834 files / 136.2 MB takes 4.0 s (task.md:45,235). Three consecutive green runs 7/7. Later heads: bc572f6 (2,370 tests) container 318.8-360.1 s vs native 475.5 s, on a machine 60-72% loaded (task.md:215-221); 19b3906 (2,472 tests) container 246.8 / 344.3 / 330.2 s (task.md:267-270).
cards.limits: Speedup is run-to-run noisy (same setting varies by +-15 s; same pass 116 s vs 200 s on a loaded machine, task.md:274). One clean sample per setting. Cause of the 1.9x on the parallel pass is INFERRED (Windows-to-container socket path), not profiled (task.md:96). Container memory/CPU not sampled; no --cpus or memory limits set, so a check can take the whole Docker VM (task.md:166). Only Docker Desktop 29.9.2 on WSL 2 on Windows verified. Never run in the main checkout. Still optional; the Windows path remains the gate (see A4-04).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Directly transferable pattern for a FastAPI+Postgres repo: run pytest in a Linux container on the DB container's network, copy the tree by stdin with a hash manifest (no bind mount, so no Windows file-share slowness), tag the image by a hash of lockfile+Dockerfile, make the check refuse to build/pull or fall back, kill the container when the host dies (stdin-EOF + init + AutoRemove, shown 0.6 s). FixFlow's backend (pytest-asyncio + asyncpg) would face the same Windows-to-Docker published-port cost. The Playwright/Chromium parts are Django-specific and can be dropped.

cards.name: Container lifetime and verification safety demonstrations
cards.what_it_is: Guards so a container check cannot outlive or silently diverge from its host: stdin pipe left open, bootstrap kills the process group and exits 143 on EOF; StdinOnce+AutoRemove; unique container name with host pid label; leftover sweep removes dead-host containers and refuses live-host ones; deadline CLINIC_CHECK_CONTAINER_SECONDS=3600; result line 'CLINIC-INNER-RESULT passed=P total=T' accepted only when total==7 and exit 0; per-checkout lock and machine-wide slot taken before copy; internal network with no internet egress; cap_drop ALL; no-new-privileges. Planted-failures demonstration (failing, erroring, skipped, xfail, xpass, serial-failing, os._exit(7)) yields CHECK FAILED 6/7.
cards.measured: Host killed with TerminateProcess: container and docker clients gone in 0.6 s; only docker client killed: 0.6 s (task.md:53,104-105). Ctrl-Break to host: exit 149, container gone in 1.2 s; killing the uv parent only left host and container running, killing host then removed container in 2.4 s (task.md:244). Hung test in container: 'no test made progress for 20s ... killed' after 24 s, no leftover process (task.md:225). Docker's own stdin behaviour was verified only on this one setup.
cards.limits: Docker Desktop stopped mid-run not run (would take down ~20 sessions' DB containers; only DOCKER_HOST at a closed port shown) (task.md:109,227). Whole-check path for a hang not run. Ctrl-C in a real console not typed. Remaining window of 0.6 s where the lock is free while tests still run (task.md:53). No hash pinning for Debian packages or the Chromium zip.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The set of fail-closed demonstrations (kill host, kill client, daemon unreachable, image missing, stale packages, planted failures) is a reusable verification checklist for any gate that wraps a container. The principle 'a gate must have an adversarial demonstration for every way it could print PASS wrongly' transfers to FixFlow's check scripts.

cards.name: The two Linux-only test failures and the Linux platform findings
cards.what_it_is: First time the suite ran on Linux it found platform defects Windows could never see. First run at 3608b8b: 2,173 tests, 2,171 passed; failures and a mypy failure were in the task's own code or devtools (P-1 9 attr-defined errors from unguarded Windows ctypes in process_guard.py; P-2 unused type:ignore on Linux; P-3 test_worker_databases assumed a unique checkout path; P-4 seven pytest parameter ids contain paths/random keys so differ between platforms; P-5 own tests). Second set after merging main at 51c8cf6: 2 of 2,472 tests failed only on Linux, both in the faster-check session's POSIX path that its own record said was 'not exercised on this PC': test_a_leftover_of_a_finished_pass_is_killed_by_terminate (test reaped the child before terminate, so on POSIX the process-group signal was skipped) and test_a_hung_process_is_killed_and_reported (child never reaped, Popen.__del__ ResourceWarning became a failure). Both fixed in the tests, assertions unchanged, product code untouched.
cards.measured: k1 run: CHECK FAILED 6/7, 2 failed, 2,315 passed (task.md:258). Collected ids Linux vs Windows: both 2,246 (later 2,370 and 2,472) in the same order; differ in exactly seven ids of test_placeholder_or_invalid_values_refuse_to_start (task.md:75,223,277). One chance-dependent finance test failed once (test_no_s07_page_period_or_as_of_gives_the_salary_funding_away[finance_operator]) (task.md:123).
cards.limits: Both failures were in code of the very session that added Linux POSIX branches, so they show 'code never run on its target OS is untested', not a general defect rate. Windows-only code (job object, msvcrt lock, socket retry) is not covered by the container mode. A platform-specific type:ignore needs unused-ignore in its list (convention proposed, task.md:118,190).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Concrete evidence that a Windows-only gate hides Linux defects; FixFlow's backend is Linux-targeted (Railway) and CI already runs on Linux, but local Windows-only runs would share the same blind spot. Transferable rules: no test assumes a unique checkout path; do not put paths or random values in parametrize ids; compare collected ids across platforms after normalising.

cards.name: Why the Linux run is not the gate (native stays the gate)
cards.what_it_is: The container mode is optional and the Windows-native check remains the gate. Reason stated in the guides: native is the only run that exercises the Windows branches (the job object that kills the container with the check, process_alive on Windows, msvcrt lock, socket-buffer retry, scratch_dir symlink workaround, os.name=='nt' test branches); a container-only gate stops covering them. Recommendation: run native when devtools or the host side of check.py changes, before a release of the tooling, and as a canary. The root was left to choose the gate ('the root's gate').
where: docs/tasks/linux-test-runner/task.md:3 (not merged into main at writing)
cards.measured: none (a design decision; the speed numbers it forgoes are in A4-01: ~230 s vs ~350 s)
cards.limits: Owner's list (B06, B18) says the Windows check is still the gate and Linux is optional, so the 1.5x speed-up is not applied by default. The tooling itself (devtools) is Windows-hosted, which is why the host side has to be exercised natively. A second maintainer on Linux/macOS: host side not run (task.md:138,163). No record that the owner or root made container mode the default.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: If FixFlow's host stays Windows, the same trade-off applies: decide explicitly which mode is the gate and which platform-specific code each mode leaves unexercised. If the gate tooling is plain Python with no Windows-specific process handling, the container can be the gate.

cards.name: Worker sweep and system-load measurements for the check
cards.what_it_is: Sweep of pytest-xdist worker counts in container mode (6, 9, 12, 16) and system load sampling every 5 s (measure.py, summarize.py); a second check beside the first with CLINIC_CHECK_NO_LOCK=1 to size the two-slot design; 8-GiB-free rule for offering the second lock slot.
cards.measured: Parallel pass by workers: 6 -> 137.5 s (clean), 9 -> 136.4, 12 -> 120.3/115.7/104.7 and 135.1/105.2/113.4, 16 -> 127.3 (task.md:87-90); knee between 6 and 12; 12 is 'defensible but not established' (~8% of whole check) (task.md:92). Load during final runs: container mean 30-37% / peak 70-77% processor, least free host memory 4.7-5.1 GB; native 31% / 63%, 5.0 GB (task.md:96). Two container checks at 12 workers each: whole 266.4 and 267.0 s vs 220 s alone (about 20% slower each), machine 50% mean / 100% peak, least free memory 5.3 GB; at 6 each: 285.9/283.0 s, 7.3 GB (task.md:98). Native 8 workers gained 3% over 6 in the faster-check record (docs/tasks/faster-check/task.md:322).
cards.limits: Noisy; one clean sample at 6 workers. Machine shared with other sessions. One of four paired runs failed on a chance-dependent test. Serial pass (about 92 s, 134 tests, mostly fixed waits in the race harness) is 40% of the container check and is deliberately NOT split (no evidence the race harness's timing assumptions survive concurrency).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Method is reusable: sweep worker count, sample whole-machine CPU and free memory every 5 s, test a pair at once before approving a second slot. A memory-gated second slot (8 GiB free) is the same mechanism the clinic repo uses to avoid the two crashes (B05).

cards.name: Local staging VM (Hyper-V rig) and the drills a-o: what each proves
cards.what_it_is: A Hyper-V gen-2 Debian 12 VM 'clinic-staging' (2 vCPU, 2 GB, 20 GB, no swap, sized like the proposed hosted VM) built by deploy/host/rig.sh (cloud image to VHDX, cloud-init seed), provisioned by deploy/vm/provision.sh (PostgreSQL 17, uv, gunicorn behind a systemd socket, nginx self-signed, hardened units, backup and cleanup timers, ufw) and deployed with versioned releases by deploy-release.sh. Drills (shell scripts in deploy/drills/): a first deploy on a clean machine; b upgrade; c backup+restore (age-encrypted set, wipe, restore, row md5 per table); d resource fit; e load (Locust, 12 clerks); f POSIX checks; g security probe; h chained release upgrades S01..HEAD with rollback; i ops/hardening checks; j volume page timings; k contention with worker SIGKILL; l restricted-figures leak scan; m refused rollback past a breaking migration; n 18 negative cases for verify_grants; o fail-closed after reboot.
where: deploy/drills/*.sh (a_first_deploy, b_upgrade, c_backup_restore, d_resource_fit, e_load, f_posix_checks, g_security_probe, h_release_rollback, i_ops_checks, j_volume, k_contention, l_restricted, m_breaking_rollback, n_grants_negatives, o_fail_closed_reboot)
cards.measured: Fresh VM serving 109 s after VM up (provision+deploy 101 s, seed 7 s) (staging-rig task.md:23). Upgrade 7 s, web down ~5 s, 780 keys preserved (task.md:24). Restore 2 s for 5.6 MB set (task.md:25). Eleven chained releases deployed onto a restored database; release 10-23 s, web unavailable 6-15 s (s11 task.md:27). Restore at 781,505 rows (90,019 documents, 274 MB, 51.5 MB set): backup 5 s, restore 14 s, 105 tables identical by row count and md5 (s11 task.md:28,58). Security probe at tree after identity follow-up: 99 PASS, 0 FAIL, 117 routes, 696 signed-in GETs (s11 task.md:195-ish GT-24). Drill o 68 PASS, 0 FAIL after round 3 (s11 task.md:~270). Drills found real defects: F-S11-2 (restore re-grants TEMPORARY), cleanup symlink follow, N9 whole documents tree in every backup, and drills' own harness faults (ssh in while-read swallowed sets; CRLF needle file made the secret scan match nothing; a piped loop in a subshell reported 'All checks passed' with failed sign-ins).
cards.limits: One PC, synthetic data, a fast desktop CPU; hosted vCPU will be slower. Proves nothing about a hosting provider, quote, offsite store, or the clinic network. Hyper-V creation needs UAC prompts that were declined twice, so the fresh-VM variant of drill c never ran (wiped target only). No second maintainer ran the scripts. Several drill rounds still needed multi-round review: the S11 slice alone needed 3 root-gate rounds + 3 Opus re-reviews, and each fix round produced new P1s (restore boundary lost in two ordinary sequences, GV-01/GV-02) - direct evidence for B01.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Pattern: a production-like rehearsal host plus numbered, re-runnable drill scripts whose results files record commit and uncommitted-file count, each with a positive control. FixFlow deploys to Railway (managed), so Hyper-V rig would not transfer, but the drill structure (clean-install first deploy, upgrade across migrations on a restored DB, backup/restore row-md5 compare, security probe, restricted-data leak scan with positive controls) and the rule 'results header names commit and dirty count' do. Directly relevant to B02 (walk a clean install end to end).

cards.name: Drill harness faults that would have produced false passes
cards.what_it_is: A recorded list of cases where the verification tooling itself reported success wrongly, found only by Opus refute-review or a failing rerun: the secret-in-logs scan wrote its needle file with CRLF so grep matched nothing (PASS proved nothing); the needle list was 9 fixed strings not the 13 accounts' secrets; drill c claimed an 81-row volume as 581,243 rows (cited file showed 1,482 rows) and '8 files' for 4; drill j ended 'All checks passed' while every sign-in failed because the failure was counted in a piped subshell loop; ssh inside while-read swallowed the list of sets; the load disturber's arithmetic took no backups; 'does not decrypt without the key' would pass for any file; drill l's positive controls passed when nobody could sign in.
where: docs/tasks/s11-operations/task.md:316-ish (section 16 'What went wrong in the drill itself')
cards.measured: none (qualitative record). Counts: S11 reviews: round 1 root gate GS-01..GS-34 (1 P1, 15 P2, 18 P3); round 2 GT-01..GT-27; round 3 GV-01..GV-06; Opus re-review 9c found six P1-by-rule items (s11 task.md:9a, 9c, 15).
cards.limits: These were caught by a reviewing model, so they are evidence for B17 (all review is model reading code): a human has not read the drill scripts. Some limits remain recorded as 'not done' (earlier-run passwords not searched).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Strong, transferable rule: every 'nothing found' check needs a positive control that must be found by the same function, and a drill must fail when its inputs are empty (no needles, no signed-in person, no layers). Also: do not let result text say PASS from a pipe that runs in a subshell; record commit and uncommitted count in each results header.

cards.name: What has never run on a real host (the real-host gap)
cards.what_it_is: An explicit, repeated list of what the local rig cannot prove: the PC-off half of T17; an independent offsite store with write-only token and retention locks (the PC held the copy); a real RTO including key custody and people; a fresh-VM restore (wiped target only); a real quote, region, domain, certificate and HSTS behaviour; certificate renewal; performance on a hosted vCPU; the clinic's network; a notification channel (watcher only exits non-zero and appends to a file); credential rotation; a second maintainer following the runbook; the stock-ledger volume (250,000 movements; ledger held 11). The runbook states it is 'not a runbook for a real host'.

cards.name: Claude Code context system: what it is (compaction steering, not a memory database)
cards.what_it_is: A standard-library Python hook package for long Claude Code sessions. It (1) sets autoCompactWindow 400000 so compaction triggers near 367k instead of the Opus 5.5 default near 967k; (2) PreCompact hook saves an immutable snapshot of declared task-state sections, a factual ledger of the window and a raw copy of the window, and injects instructions into the summariser; (3) SessionStart(source=compact) restores the snapshot verbatim and reports sections changed on disk since; (4) PostCompact archives the summary; (5) one nudge per cycle ~40k tokens before the threshold; (6) PreToolUse Read admission (files over 30 KB return a first page of ~16 KB/120 lines plus an outline of up to 60 entries); (7) ctx.py recall search/show for exact text. Install writes hooks to settings.local.json, window and precomputeCompactionEnabled=false to settings.json, rules to .claude/rules/context-system.md. It does not store a graph or database; it steers native compaction and keeps files.
cards.measured: README.md:3 states 'built and checked offline (85 regression tests, harness dry run). Not installed in this project and not yet run in a live session.' docs/tasks/context-admission-research/task.md:14: tests 85/85, repro_v3.py 35/35; 'Hook run time on the real transcripts is 0.1-0.2 s'. Quality at 300-400k vs full history is stated unmeasured (README.md:3). Pause length of each synchronous compaction 'unmeasured' (README.md limits).
cards.limits: Never installed or run in a live session; the live quality comparison was never run (task.md status line 3). Relies on undocumented Claude Code 2.1.293 behaviour (PreCompact stdout merged into summariser instructions; README Limits). Hooks fire for subagent compactions too without saying whose (hooks.py:1-15). Interpreter path stored in machine-local settings; hooks stop silently if it moves. Targets a single long interactive session's context size, not multi-session orchestration.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Directly relevant to B04 (orchestrator context overflow and summarisation): the restore-declared-sections-verbatim pattern plus 'summariser told exactly which sections are covered' would let FixFlow's orchestrator survive compaction without losing the Decisions / Ruled out / Next action sections of docs/tasks/<id>/task.md. FixFlow already has the same task.md convention. Needs a live check on the current Claude Code version before trusting it.

cards.name: Data model and storage format: files, not SQLite, not a graph
cards.what_it_is: Plain-file storage. Claude version: per snapshot a triplet under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/context-system/ named s{seq:04d}-c{cycle:03d}-{utcstamp}: -restore.md (text to restore), -meta.json (seq, cycle, tag, created, boundaries, tokens, peak, state_file, state_sha, mode, covered blocks with sha+text, ledger_path; written LAST as the commit point), -ledger.md, optional raw window JSONL copy, markers -superseded and -consumed. State file is markdown with headings or <!-- ctx:restore --> blocks. Config is config.json. Codex adapter: one immutable JSON file per journal event (events/event_########_<32hex>.json with text, text_sha, payload, payload_sha) and per snapshot (snapshots/snapshot_########_<32hex>.json), plus a control.json per session, written by storage.write_json(immutable=True) under locks. Recall is a linear scan of JSONL transcripts and .md archive notes with a needle prefilter; no index, no embeddings, no graph, no SQLite. The only 'tree-like' structures are the heading list of the state file and the transcript record sequence.
cards.measured: Search speed: docs/tasks/context-admission-research/task.md:14 'recall over all 211 real transcripts (115 MB) takes about 1 s'. Codex storage stress: eval_storage_stress ran 1, 4, 8, 16 spawned processes, 464 events and 464 snapshots, exact counts, hashes and session isolation (tools/context_system_codex/RESULTS_2026-10-12.md, Mechanics section). Search cost at 100/1,000/10,000 events was planned (EVALUATION_PLAN.md ~line 296) but no result was found.
cards.limits: Grep over whole history scales linearly with history; no ranking beyond term count and recency (recall.py:190-205 _score); no semantic or structural retrieval. Cannot answer relational questions (which decision superseded which, what depends on what).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The immutable-file-per-event plus checksum plus 'meta written last as commit point' pattern is portable and avoids a database dependency. 1 s to scan 115 MB is a useful baseline: a SQLite/graph index only pays off beyond that scale or for relational queries. Directly answers the owner's question: no SQLite graph exists in this lane.

cards.name: Recall: exact search plus show, no model calls
cards.what_it_is: ctx.py recall search '<terms>' scans main transcripts, nested subagent/workflow transcripts and the archive (window copies, ledgers, summaries, snapshots). Requires at least ceil(n/2) of the words (needed = (len+1)//2), supports quoted phrases and kind and session filters, ranks by distinct terms then recency, dedups records by uuid across live and archived copies, one hit per archive note. Every reference is path:line:block (or #paragraph) so recall show <ref> opens exactly the matched record, paged by chars/offset. Local only. Codex variant: bounded 2,048-byte responses with paged text, provenance, integrity hashes and session-bound cursors, over a journal of prompts, tool results, assistant messages and subagent results (not Codex's unstable transcript).
where: tools/context_system/templates/rules.md (habit: search exact history before re-reading)
cards.measured: 1 s over 211 transcripts / 115 MB (docs/tasks/context-admission-research/task.md:14). Token saving from recall: none measured. In the 2026-10-14 screen 'No arm used journal recall' (tools/context_system_codex/RESULTS_2026-10-14.md:36-37), so no live evidence of retrieval benefit.
cards.limits: Lexical only; no semantic match, no staleness or supersession awareness; depends on the model choosing to search; no evidence recall saves tokens versus re-reading. Codex journal begins only at hook activation, no import of earlier conversations, no cross-session search.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Cheap and dependency-free; the stable-reference scheme (path:line:block) is the transferable part, since it lets an agent cite and reopen evidence. For FixFlow a lexical scan across .claude project transcripts would also help B12 (verify what a session really said), but only if sessions actually use it.

cards.name: Declared-state restoration contract (whole-or-nothing blocks, immutable snapshots, one-time restore)
cards.what_it_is: Design rules paid for by successive adversarial reviews. Only task-state the file declares is restored: text between <!-- ctx:restore --> markers, else the whole file if small, else whole sections whose heading is exactly one of config restore_sections (Next action, Current state, User instructions and corrections, Decisions, Ruled out, Open questions...). Blocks restored whole or not at all; nothing is cut after the summariser has been told it is covered; summariser obligations are never truncated. Snapshots are immutable, ordered by per-session seq, bound to the transcript compaction-boundary count, restored at most once, no wall-clock expiry. After restore, covered blocks are diffed against disk and changed ones reported with current text. Project root from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; focus is per session; paths outside root rejected. Snapshot cap 9,000 chars, restore total 9,800 (hook strings capped at 10,000 by Claude Code).
cards.measured: Offline only: 85 tests in tests/test_context_system.py (structure: classes RestoreCandidatesTest, SnapshotTest, ChangedOnDiskTest, SummaryTest, LedgerTest, StateFileTest, RecallTest, CompactionConfigTest, HookEntryTest, ReadAdmissionTest, NudgeTest, InstallTest, FocusCliTest, RealTranscriptTest); repro_v3.py 35/35; defects reproduced then fixed: 6 (first external review) + 15 (first adversarial) + 22 (wave 1) + 10 (wave 2) (task.md:14). Ruled out in task.md: keyword heading matching ('Spending' matched 'pending'), time-based snapshot expiry (refused valid snapshots), project-wide focus pointer (leaked one session's task into another).
cards.limits: Verified on synthetic cases and copies of two real transcripts only; not in a live session. Quality of continuation after restore never measured on Claude. Wave-2 optional adversarial pass left open (task.md Next action item 5).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The negative rules (no keyword matching, no time expiry, per-session focus, restore whole-or-nothing, tell the summariser exactly what is covered) transfer as design constraints for any compaction or handoff hook FixFlow builds for its orchestrator; they were each found by a reproduced defect, so they are cheap lessons.

cards.name: Read admission and context-hygiene rules (token saving at the source)
cards.what_it_is: Two token-saving levers aimed at what bloats the window. PreToolUse hook rewrites a Read of a file over large_read_bytes (30,000) with no offset/limit into a limit giving the first ~16 KB (min 120 lines) plus an outline (md headings, py/js/ts definitions, max 60 entries, thinned by sampling). templates/rules.md habits: main thread orchestrates; whole-document reading and log trawls go to subagents returning at most ~2,500 characters with path:line evidence and longer output to a file; files over ~300 lines are created by a subagent or generator, never rewritten in full twice (use Edit); reusable scripts run from a file path; workflows re-run with scriptPath; a draft written to a file is not also printed; keep task.md current; search exact history before re-deriving.
cards.measured: Forensics of two real sessions (output/context-system-research/evidence-2026-10-10/forensics_session1.json): session 2d443524 start 78,450 tokens, peak 731,239, 198 API calls, 0 compactions; thinking blocks 205,329 tokens (31.5%), Write file content 90,710 (13.9%), Edit payloads 48,302 (7.4%); tools/reapply.py written in full twice (24k and 25k chars). task.md:11: sessions peaked 731,239 and 869,982; 53-69% of growth is the model's own retained output (thinking 25-31%, Write/Edit about 20%), tool results 30-40%. Read admission itself: saving not measured; hook has unit tests (ReadAdmissionTest).
cards.limits: The forensics show most growth is the model's own output, which Read admission does not touch; only compaction removes retained thinking. Rules are habits in a rules file, not enforced. Not installed, so no measured effect.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The forensic breakdown method (categorise retained tokens by source from usage.output_tokens_details and block types) is reusable on FixFlow sessions to find what actually fills the orchestrator context. The 'subagent returns <=2,500 chars and writes the rest to a file' rule targets B16 directly (subagents cannot write files in the clinic setup, so they return through the orchestrator context; here the rule assumes they can write).

cards.name: Why native compaction was chosen as foundation, and the compaction-trigger facts
cards.what_it_is: Binary and docs investigation (Claude Code 2.1.293, later 2.1.295) establishing: Opus 5.5 default window 1M, auto-compaction threshold = window minus 20k reserved minus 13k = 967,000; autoCompactWindow (100000-1000000) in project or local settings moves the trigger (400000 gives ~367k; a trigger, not a ceiling, one step can overshoot); per-model modelSettings autoCompactWindow needs v2.1.288+; desktop launches the CLI with --setting-sources=user,project,local so project settings load; order at compaction is PreCompact, summary, SessionStart(compact), boundary written, PostCompact; precomputeCompactionEnabled false disables early PreCompact paths; hook string cap 10,000 UTF-16 units; compaction hooks also fire for subagent compactions with the main session id and no agent_id. Decision: native compaction is the foundation because only compaction removes retained thinking and old file payloads; output filtering alone could not hold 300-400k.
cards.measured: Transcript facts: 0 compact_boundary records in the 870k session; 967,000 threshold derived from the binary (native.json summary). 'Status' is 'in_use' only for the finding; the hook package that exploits it is not installed.
cards.limits: Facts are version-specific (2.1.293; strings present in 2.1.295 but not proof of identical behaviour). Whether project autoCompactWindow reaches the desktop session was not traced in code (task.md Current state). Claude Code updates silently.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The trigger arithmetic and the 'autoCompactWindow in project settings reaches the desktop app' finding apply directly to FixFlow orchestrator sessions on the same PC and could reduce B04 overflow events with a one-line settings change. Re-verify on the current version before relying on it.

cards.name: Claude A/B evaluation harness (system vs native vs handoff vs reference), never run live
cards.what_it_is: tools/context_system/eval: a generated fictional water-utility meter-reconciliation project with a script of user turns carrying planted items (instructions, two corrections, a decision with reason, two rejected approaches, conversation-only facts, early-file facts, distant evidence, unfinished work). Four arms in separate sandboxes: system, native (window only), handoff (old manual handoff loop past 300k), reference (no compaction, only with --size fit). Follow-up tasks E1-E4 run twice each (resume on a fork; fresh session) from a snapshot, scored deterministically by rules in scoring.py (9 categories, no model judge). Profiles: quality (Opus 5.5 xhigh, ultracode, window 400k, 3 compactions) and mechanics (Sonnet 5.5 low, window 150k, 1 compaction). Dry run exits 0 only if every section passes.
where: tools/context_system/eval/harness/ (driver, scenario, scoring, metrics, estimate, dryrun, simulate)
cards.measured: Dry run: 175 checks, about 65 s, fails when faults are injected (task.md:15). Forecast, with every constant an assumption: quality comparison 156M to 512M tokens total (three arms), 208M to 698M with reference arm; mechanics check about 3M to 10M (eval/README.md Estimated usage table). No live run: the bundled CLI reported loggedIn false (task.md:15).
cards.limits: Never executed against a model; the forecast is the cost barrier (hundreds of millions of cache-read tokens). One scenario, one run per arm would not support a general claim (eval/README.md What a result can show). Scripted user. Print mode, not the desktop app.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The method (planted-item scenario, forked-branch resume vs fresh restart, deterministic scorer with no model judge, snapshot-and-restore between tasks) is a reusable way to test any memory or handoff mechanism, including FixFlow's task.md restore. The cost forecast is a warning: a quality comparison at 400k windows is prohibitively expensive.

cards.name: Research survey of shipped memory systems (MemTree/Infinite, Virtual Context, YesMem, LCM, Rolling Context, Distil, Parsec, Jev, Scalpel)
cards.what_it_is: Source-pinned audit (commits and npm/PyPI versions pinned; verification.json holds hashes) of external systems against the requirement 'about 300-400k active tokens carrying the quality of an ~800k history'. Initial report selected Claude Code Infinite 1.0.14 with MemTree as the closest shipped match, with Virtual Context 0.6 as configurable alternative. Distinguishes: CCC_COMPACT_TARGET=350k does not lower the 800k trigger; CCC_BUDGET_TOKENS=400k is documented test-only. A later decision in the task file superseded this: MemTree ruled out (terminal-only wrapper, paid hosted service receiving all tool output, vendor-only benchmark); 'no GitHub system is adopted' and the local hook system was built instead.
cards.measured: Third-party figures only: MemTree 68.7/100 vs full-history 69.3/100 vs native-compact-first 48.7/100; total input 39M vs 113M vs 17M tokens; time 11-22 vs 24-54 minutes (Opus 5.5, ~775k history compressed to ~420k, 3 rounds; report.md:23-27, flagged as within a 10-point noise floor and not reproducible, run transcripts unpublished). Parsec (SWE-bench, Sonnet 4.6, baseline ~80k context): 62 vs 57 of 100 solved, cost -39%, input tokens -54%, wall time -25%, peak context 41.4k vs 79.8k (surgery-and-quality-contracts.md:43), vendor-operated. Distil own pilot: 4.5% smaller prompts per step, 9.7% more cost on six tasks (report.md:53). Local: Infinite 89/89 mocked tests (infinite-and-yesmem.md:23), mechanics only.
cards.limits: No installation, no live trial, no history upload. All quality evidence is vendor-reported, small, not at the requested scale. Corpus-specific selection criteria and the squeez-first recommendation of earlier reports are marked superseded (README.md).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Source for the design vocabulary the owner may be recalling (summary DAG, topic hierarchy, BM25 plus embeddings, expand-on-demand, stable cached prefix). Useful for the harness-ideas line: the key lesson is that token reduction alone did not equal lower cost or equal outcomes (Headroom: 44% more cost; RTK 13% more; surgery-and-quality-contracts.md:43), and that the native-compact-first arm lost 20 points of quality in the one reported test.

cards.name: Codex adapter: PreCompact snapshot and compact-start restore with byte budgets and a journal
cards.what_it_is: A port of the Claude system to local Codex (tools/context_system_codex), adapted only from the completed harness. Seven project-local hooks merged into .codex/hooks.json; PreCompact saves an immutable checksummed snapshot of selected task-state blocks (native summary unchanged); SessionStart(source=compact) returns the saved text; startup/resume supplies focus and recall commands. A journal of prompts, tool results, assistant completions and subagent results with provenance serves search/show; byte budgets (snapshot_bytes, restore_bytes, recall_bytes; envelope bytes including JSON framing and final newline) in budget.py; defaults 6,000-char snapshot cap and 9,000-char restore cap, recall 2,048 bytes per response, configuration cannot exceed 20,000. Handles repeat callbacks, concurrent processes, absent transcripts, damaged data; failures degrade to native behaviour with a visible 'checkpoint unavailable' message. Native thresholds, summariser prompt and permissions unchanged.
cards.measured: Tests: 40 (39 pass, 1 skip) on 2026-10-11; 136 (134 pass, 2 symlink skips) on 2026-10-12 (README.md Verification, RESULTS_2026-10-12.md); 151 (149, 2 skips) on 2026-10-14 (RESULTS_2026-10-14.md:51-52); 244 tests, 242 pass, 2 skipped, 18.039 s on 2026-10-15 (RESULTS_2026-10-15.md:125-126). Storage stress 1/4/8/16 spawned processes: 464 events and 464 snapshots, exact counts (RESULTS_2026-10-12.md). Live mechanics: three manual compactions per arm, both native and adapter 15/15 facts; adapter captured 3 PreCompact, 3 PostCompact, 3 compact-start events and 3 snapshots (README.md Live verification).
cards.limits: The cinema pilot (a different project) was the live target; Codex, not Claude Code. No retention or efficiency gain shown (see A5-11..A5-14). Concurrent parent/child compaction untested. README says no retention/prune command exists in the first adapter, and large reads are only a habit, not a rewritten command.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: FixFlow uses Claude Code not Codex, so the adapter code does not transfer; the engineering rules do (byte-cap the complete hook envelope, immutable checksummed snapshots, visible fallback to native on any failure, never claim coverage you cannot prove).

cards.name: Evaluation run 2026-10-12: first work pilot and mechanics probes
cards.what_it_is: One paired scenario: booking policy changed twice, an unrelated inventory audit, then resumed booking work after two manual compactions; native baseline vs adapter; gpt-6-astra at ultra effort, 32k trigger, hidden checks, agent-maintained blank state. Plus an automatic-compaction probe, a delegated-worker usage probe and storage stress.
cards.measured: Artifact score 100/100 both arms; ordinary reported cumulative input native 300,801 vs adapter 331,815 tokens (+10.31%, summary json:9,15,42); median request input 12,070 vs 13,525 (json:10,15); restored text 2,533 and 3,307 bytes, envelopes 2,655 and 3,436 bytes (json:17-21); hook duration median 2,120 ms, max 2,205 ms (json:39-40); child probe 9,931 reported input (json:51); stage spend 984,984 input and 14,629 output of a 1M/40k soft cap (json:54-57). context_gain_proven false (json:61).
cards.limits: One scenario pair, no confidence claim (json:60). Compaction model usage unreported so full-run saving unknown (json:59). Second pair, budget frontier and held-out confirmation deferred (json:63-68). An evaluator timing error (verifier expected restore before the continuation) stopped one run and was recorded as not a memory failure.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Establishes the baseline lesson that a restore layer costs about 10% more input than native in a small case while preserving the same artifact score; a restored checkpoint is an insurance, not a saving. Hook launch of about 2 s is a tax FixFlow should measure before adding per-event hooks.

cards.name: Evaluation run 2026-10-13/14: three-way screen (native N, maintained notes M, adapter A) and overhead profile
cards.what_it_is: Fresh synthetic retry-worker repair task with changing evidence, corrected policy and target, and intervening audits; gpt-6-astra/ultra, 20k automatic trigger, 3 KiB note ceiling, 450k input / 12k output soft cap per task. Verdict recorded: inconclusive_all_arms_unfinished, stop larger live expansion. Plus a model-free overhead profile of hook launch cost.
cards.measured: Partial completion score N 76.19, M 76.19, A 71.43 (RESULTS_2026-10-14.md:21-23); reported input 456,586 / 462,765 / 455,234; output 12,038 / 9,015 / 7,570; automatic compactions 3 / 3 / 2; median request input A 13,495 vs N 13,789 vs M 14,701.5 (lines 33-35); adapter restore envelopes 2,406 and 2,979 bytes (line 42). Budget: all four attempts 1,480,227 input and 30,111 output vs 1.5M/40k limits (lines 70-71). Time: wall 16,888.984 s including a 14,227-s suspended gap; awake 2,661.859 s; original two-hour wall limit breached and amended (lines 76-80). Overhead: in-process hook+storage median 4.9 ms (4.862 in json), direct Python startup 71 ms, registered Windows wrapper 243 ms (RESULTS lines 54-56; overhead-report json); earlier native hook duration ~2.1 s only partly explained. Offline tests 151 (149 pass, 2 skip).
cards.limits: All arms hit the cap unfinished, so no completed control exists and context saving cannot be computed (RESULTS lines 28-30). Journal recall not used (lines 36-37). Controlled file-tool facade lacked ordinary shell and calculation tools, so repeated reads and note writing dominated usage (lines 94-97). A host suspension (Windows sleep) broke one run; a temporary idle-sleep prevention was added. A raw runner label 'adapter_quality_gate_failed' contradicted the plan's 'inconclusive' and was corrected offline with raw evidence kept.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Operational lessons for long agent runs on the same Windows PC: a host sleep/suspend mid-run yields a spurious timeout (14,227-s gap, websocket idle timeout) and SetThreadExecutionState was used to prevent it; hook wrapper cost is ~243 ms (not 2 s) so the earlier 2 s was runtime overhead. Pre-register verdict labels in the plan so a harness cannot mislabel its own stop. Do not start a gain study until a completed competent control exists.

cards.name: Evaluation run 2026-10-15: persistent-session retention study (final), including the aggregate delivery gate failure
cards.what_it_is: Persistent local Codex sessions, three arms, two automatic compactions each at the native default threshold, two controller-supplied bulky tool outputs to fill history (each targeting 0.94 reported capacity), then two no-tool recall probes (8 and 7 disjoint facts) and an executable repair task. Seed 1732. Preceded by failed attempts: retention final report stopped 'Turn did not complete' (retention-final-report-2026-10-14.json:1663-1666, reported input 150,604), tool-pressure report stopped 'Full pressure admission could not be established before compaction' (tool-pressure-report-2026-10-14.json:1750-1757, 1,913,648 reported input including earlier), a 'giant user-message' carryover and dynamic-tool clipping error, standalone pressure stopped 'Turn did not complete' (standalone-pressure-report:1325-1332).
cards.measured: Recall 15/15 and practical task 100% in all three arms (RESULTS_2026-10-15.md:11-15 table). Ordinary input N 720,036; M 794,310; A 842,620; output 2,471 / 4,327 / 6,232 (lines 13-15). Adapter +6.08% over M, +17.02% over N (line 22). Probe request input N 11,387/11,680; M 11,853/12,277; A 13,569/12,869 (lines 27-30). Fall from about 250k to 11-14k occurred in all arms through native compaction, not attributable to the adapter (lines 32-35). Adapter authored notes 2,263 bytes; selected checkpoint envelope 2,894 B both boundaries; additional startup envelope 2,068 B at boundary 1; combined 4,962 B vs a 4 KiB gate, so the aggregate gate FAILED at boundary 1 (lines 64-73). Usage: all current-study attempts 4,350,448 input and 22,764 output (line 106; audit json:3179-3180); cohort 2,356,966 / 13,030 (line 105); remaining allowance 649,552 / 37,236 (line 109). Interruptions: N hit the account limit during its second remote compaction, A during its first (lines 78-80). Active time 2,152.036 s (line 96). Tests 244, 242 pass, 2 skip, 18.039 s (lines 125-126). Archive: 101 byte-verified files (line 118).
cards.limits: Interrupted exploratory cohort, not statistical evidence (lines 23-24); no uninterrupted latency comparison; remote compaction usage and billing excluded so economic efficiency unknown (lines 109-111); desktop UI equivalence, broader coding conversations and a 2/4/8 KiB frontier not established (lines 53-56). The first completed adapter boundary exposed a verifier bug (selected startup callback 42, missed checkpoint callback 44); the original false rejection is retained and a corrected matcher declared before any adapter quality result.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Model-quality result is a negative for 'memory restore beats native compaction plus a maintained notes file': equal recall and task success, more tokens. The transferable point for FixFlow is that a disciplined 3 KiB task file (arm M) already matches the adapter, so the cheapest lever is the notes convention FixFlow already has (task.md). Also: usage limits interrupted two arms mid-compaction (B03); the harness handled resume of the same persistent session without replaying completed facts.

cards.name: Final independent audit and overall verdict on the Codex line
cards.what_it_is: A zero-model-call offline audit of the final cohort by reading supported event logs (final-independent-audit-2026-10-15.json, 252 KB, top-level keys: model_calls, source_report, manifest, prior_audit, channel_audit, episodes, reported_input_including_all_attempts, reported_output_including_all_attempts, cohort_reported_usage, complete_cohort, fresh_thread_ids_verified, normal_window_verified, adapter_delivery_verified, failures, stopped_by, soft_budget_overshoot, context_gain_proven, statistical_confirmation, historical_qualification, qualified_* fields). Verdict recorded in RESULTS_2026-10-15: 'working exact-state restoration with unproven incremental value'; no justification for a GPU summarizer, service expansion or a high-context-gain claim.
cards.measured: model_calls 0 (audit json:2); complete_cohort true; fresh_thread_ids_verified true; failures [] ; stopped_by null (json:3185-3190); context_gain_proven false (json:3198); statistical_confirmation false (json:3199); normal_window_verified false unqualified (json:3187) but qualified_normal_window_verified true (json:5336); adapter_delivery_verified false unqualified (json:3188), qualified_adapter_delivery_verified true (json:5495); qualified_historical_error_count 2 (json:5334) and qualified_local_verifier_correction_count 1 (json:5712); uninterrupted_matched_comparison false (json:5337); all_adapter_pre_model_context_within_restore_cap false (json:5713); soft_budget_overshoot input 0 output 0 (json:3192-3195); reported input incl. all attempts 4,350,448, output 22,764 (json:3179-3180).

cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The audit pattern (a separate zero-model-call pass over raw event logs that independently re-verifies a session's own claims, preserving unqualified failure flags next to qualified ones) is a direct, transferable answer to B12 (reports overstate): evidence is verified from event logs, not self-report.

cards.name: Evaluation plan with pre-registered gates and staged budgets (never met)
cards.what_it_is: EVALUATION_PLAN.md (status: proposed, 2026-10-11) defines honest units (restored bytes vs wire bytes vs tokens; never assume four chars per token), four arms (D native default, N native small threshold, M task-file control, A full adapter), and proposed gates: quality preserved (A keeps >=95% of D's score, lower CI bound above -5 points), working input at least 50% lower median request input, whole-episode cumulative input at least 25% lower, adapter must beat both N and M or recommend the simpler workflow, hook p95 under 1 second and end-to-end median at most 25% slower, no critical failures. Staged: stage 0 offline; stage 1 pilot (<=6 episodes, 1M input, 40k output, one hour); stage 2 development (<=24 episodes, 8M input, 250k output, 8 h); stage 3 held-out confirmation (60 paired blocks, 180 episodes); stage 4 long-session and failure stress. Includes rules: stop on invalid telemetry, no repeated retries of quality failures, 'inconclusive' at budget exhaustion; a future local GPU summariser or reranker only if a measured selection/retrieval bottleneck justifies it.
cards.measured: Plan is proposed targets only; no stage 2 or later was run. Actuals: stage 1 spent 984,984 input (cap 1,000,000); the 2026-10-14 screen spent 1,480,227 of 1.5M; 2026-10-15 study spent 4,350,448 of a 5M allocation (RESULTS_2026-10-15.md:106,109,113). Gate outcomes: working-input gate (-50%) not met (adapter +10.31%, +17.02%); whole-episode gate (-25%) not met; adapter-beats-M gate not met (recall equal, tokens +6.08%).
cards.limits: The plan itself says it launched no live runs. The proposed 50% and 25% targets were described in RESULTS_2026-10-12.md as not supported by the pilot.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A ready template for evaluating any memory or harness change: pre-register gates and budgets, charge all overhead (maintenance, recall, retries) to the treatment, and compare against a plain task-file control, accepting 'use the simpler workflow' as a valid result.
