cards.name: Resource and reliability findings from the evaluation drivers (host sleep, quota stops, resume, guards)
cards.what_it_is: Recorded operational failures and their handling in the eval drivers: Windows host suspension created a 14,227-second gap and a websocket idle timeout (RESULTS_2026-10-14.md:62-68), fixed by a temporary SetThreadExecutionState idle-sleep prevention cleared on exit; account usage limit hit mid-compaction for two arms (RESULTS_2026-10-15.md:78-80), resumed in the same persistent session without replaying completed work; a Windows extended-path alias race in the stress verifier (RESULTS_2026-10-12.md, Corrections section); an earlier Windows storage-stress access-denied failure kept as historical evidence (RESULTS_2026-10-15.md:126-128); soft token caps with in-flight overshoot (N 6,586, M 12,765, A 5,234 input over 450k, RESULTS_2026-10-14.md:72) and mid-turn usage monitoring and interrupts; continuous persistence of run state before and after each step and a --continue command (Claude harness eval/README.md, Stopping and continuing); driver guards (eval_guard.py, retention_guard.py, retention_pressure_guard.py) and byte-verified evidence archive.
cards.measured: Wall time 16,888.984 s vs awake 2,661.859 s (RESULTS_2026-10-14.md:76-79); 14,227.125 s suspended gap (evaluation-summary-2026-10-14.json time block); soft-cap overshoot figures as above. No memory or CPU profile of the drivers themselves was found.
cards.limits: These are single-PC observations in the Codex harness; none diagnoses the clinic's two unclean shutdowns (B05) and none measured memory pressure. The sleep/suspend cause was confirmed against independent Windows sleep/wake records (RESULTS_2026-10-14.md:62-65), which is a diagnostic method B05 never used.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Two transferable techniques: (1) correlate a long unexplained gap in an event log with Windows sleep/wake records before blaming the agent or the network (B09, B14); (2) persist run state before and after each step so a limit stop (B03) is resumable, with a --continue entry point.

result.lane: A6: corpus map and context-admission research (output/corpus-map-justification/ 00-10, docs/repo-context-audit.md, docs/technical-plan/reading-coverage.md)

cards.name: The corpus map: what problem it was to solve
cards.what_it_is: A persisted, versioned map of the clinic's markdown PLAN (not the code): for any architecture, what it depends on, what it derives from, the reasoning steps between, exact source line spans, and explicit gaps and read/linked/unresolved coverage. Motive (SESSION_STATE.md section 1): make the accumulated planning usable inside bounded working contexts so a coding agent does not load the whole corpus or trust a prose summary. Three reading methods were pre-rejected as R1 one big window, R2 split-and-merge prose summaries, R3 similarity retrieval as context; and three store shapes as R4 equality-join only, R5 one edge type, R6 two-label closed inventory (00-constraints.md). The constraint block says outright that the pass designs a METHOD, does not build the map and does not judge whether it is worth building.
cards.measured: Corpus scope for the operational prototype: 11 files, 167,342 bytes, about 41.7k tokens (09-operational/validation/contract.md:section 1; corpus-manifest.json). Nothing measured about whether the map improved any agent's work (see A6-10).
cards.limits: Plan documents only (11 files); no code, no tests, no runtime facts. The corpus is small enough to fit in one window; contract.md section 10 admits the budget bound is artificial. No clinic application exists, so implementation-quality improvement is untested. Owner wrote both cases and prototype.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The problem statement (sparse cross-file dependency and derivation in a large doc set, need for source spans and visible gaps) is real for FixFlow's CLAUDE.md, docs/*, 0001-0046 migrations and PLAYBOOK, but FixFlow's docs are already index-routed and much smaller in relation-density. Transfer the requirements list, not the whole method.

cards.name: Justification pass: quote-verified literature pack and gated research method
cards.what_it_is: A 3-day research procedure (2026-10-06 to 07): 8 lane agents harvested literature (argument graphs, discourse inventories, identity layer, provenance, stores/queries, failure modes, coverage ledgers, extraction/kinds); a deterministic reducer (tools/reduce.py) re-fetched every source itself and exact-substring-verified each quote; an independent annotator froze a pilot chain; one reasoner wrote a design; one skeptic attacked it with 21 counterexamples; one response round, then stop. Gates G0-G5 were re-run by the orchestrator rather than taken from the role's own report, and role isolation was audited from transcripts (reads only allowed inputs). Pre-registration by SHA-256 of constraint block, pilot, criteria and plans.
cards.measured: 310 findings from 89 works; 575 of 579 quotes verified by exact match against the reducer's own re-fetch; 304 findings supported (06-final/report.md:14). Per lane quotes verified: L1 77/77, L2 86/86, L3 56/56, L4 80/84, L5 77/77, L6 63/63, L7 48/48, L8 88/88 (report.md section 3 table). The 4 unverified quotes all come from one source the reducer could not fetch (a PMC captcha/403). Reproducible commands are given at report.md end.
cards.limits: Verifies that a quote exists in the source, not that the finding is correct (report: 'gates check completeness, not correctness'). All roles are models; the model closed no counterexample. Seven incidents recorded in run.md (account session limits killed six lanes; a resumed workflow replayed nothing and re-ran agents that edited prior files; edits had to be recovered from transcripts and reversed). Seeds such as Kruchten 2004 remain unread (unresolved.md section C).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Strongly transferable as an anti-overstatement control: a deterministic script that re-fetches or re-reads the cited source and exact-matches every quoted evidence string, plus orchestrator-rerun gates and transcript audits of which files a role opened. Directly answers 'session reports overstate'. Cost of the 8-lane literature harvest is not recorded, so it should be applied narrowly (verify quotes in agent reports), not as a research ritual.

cards.name: Design v1/v2: status model S1-S6, doors D1-D12, kinds, identity, gaps
cards.what_it_is: A 99-rule design (04-design/design.md, SHA f6e561fc; frozen original design.v1.md c760a1a9). Every record gets one status at creation that never changes: S1 attested by a source span, S2 codebook decision (analyst vocabulary), S3 overlay (analyst identity decision), S4 reconstructed premise on a gap, S5 candidate (similarity/alias proposal), S6 derived query result. Relation kinds are open labels (the file's own words) with three declared properties: direction, consequence in {fails_to_build, fails_to_follow, fails_to_resolve, none}, walkable. A kind without properties is inert (stored, not walked, no gaps). Identity is S1 only by explicit textual statement. Gaps are derived, keyed per (edge, slot, level, codebook version). Query levels L1=S1, L2=S1+S2, L3=L2+S3 with every analyst hop labelled; S5 never appears at any level. Three reading passes per file: introductions, cues, slots.
cards.measured: 99 numbered rules: 55 borrowed from verified quotes, 44 marked 'required: no source covers it' (06-final/report.md:7). Rejection check: 64 candidate formalisms plus this design = 401 cells, 197 pass, 192 N/A, 12 fail (report.md section 2). The design's self-scoring on R1-R6 and D1-D11 is the reasoner's own assessment; the skeptic is the only test.
cards.limits: It is a graph (typed edges between named referents) but defined as a method, not an implementation; nothing in the design names a database. Packaging is 'one store with five partitions and ten operations' (PK-1, PK-2) and is storage-agnostic. 37 unresolved items listed verbatim in 06-final/unresolved.md. Several tests of the constraint block itself (shared-constraint links such as '$8') are left to the owner. Adoption is a pending owner decision.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The status discipline is the transferable core: never let a similarity or inferred link be stored as an attested fact; derived results are recomputed, never stored; analyst/model decisions are separate records with who, when and span in view. Maps onto FixFlow's invariant that guessed state must not harden into a fact. The kind-property machinery is likely too heavy for FixFlow.

cards.name: Storage format of the operational map: JSONL partitions, no SQLite
cards.what_it_is: The built prototype (09-operational/tools/cmap.py, 78,762 bytes, plus test_cmap.py) keeps a store directory of append-only JSON-lines files: s1.jsonl (S1 attested records: edge, intro, name, clause, header, claim, untyped, idscheme, reldef, identity), s2.jsonl (codebook decisions), s3.jsonl (identity decisions), s4.jsonl (empty), candidates.jsonl (S5), chunks.jsonl + ledger.json + ledger_events.jsonl + rejects.jsonl (coverage ledger), manifest.json, reconciliation.json, plus incoming/ per-chunk reader outputs and analyst/ batches. Derived results (S6) are not stored. An S1 edge record carries file, version SHA-256, line span, exact quote, actor, rule id and chunk. cmap.py docstring: 'Run with python -I -B cmap.py <command> --store DIR'. Commands: init, chunks, chunk-show, ingest, validate, resolve, worklist, decide, context, find, show, chain, gaps, status, coverage, refresh.
cards.measured: Line counts of the store files (wc -l): s1.jsonl 3,361; s2.jsonl 154; s3.jsonl 372; s4.jsonl 0; candidates.jsonl 1,906; chunks.jsonl 51; ledger_events.jsonl 67; rejects.jsonl 0. s1.jsonl is 2,201,401 bytes for a 167,342-byte corpus. SESSION_STATE.md:53 records 3,013 reader records, 0 rejected, 2 automatic links, 291 structural records, 57 D-RECON edges, 1,906 candidates, and 11 synthetic mechanism tests passing (SESSION_STATE.md section 4).
cards.limits: Plain files, scanned whole by the CLI; no index, no SQL, no graph engine. s1.jsonl is about 13 times the corpus size. Python run requires an interpreter that is not on PATH (SESSION_STATE.md section 5). A synthetic-graph test suite is the only code test; no screen/real-use test. No cost (time, tokens) of the build was recorded.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Direct answer to the owner's recollection: this is the repository's graph-of-the-repo artifact, and it is JSON-lines, not SQLite. The record shape (id, status, file, version hash, lines, quote, actor) and the chunk-hash identity are portable to a SQLite table if FixFlow wants queries, but no SQLite version of it exists here to reuse.

cards.name: Operational map construction: bounded chunk readers, deterministic structural pass, analyst batches
cards.what_it_is: Build procedure of METHOD.md section 3: init chunks the corpus by heading section (merged small sections, at most 6,000 characters, tables split at row boundaries with header carried as read-only context); a deterministic structural pass records headings, mermaid nodes and arrows, table row keys, bare links as automated S1 records; one fresh reader agent per chunk sees only READER.md plus its chunk and writes incoming/<chunk>.jsonl; validate dry-runs; ingest sequentially is the only step that writes S1; resolve rebuilds the candidate index and ledger; worklists feed analyst agents (ANALYST.md) that decide S3 identity (same/different/cannot tell, split of lists such as USER-04/05) and S2 vocabulary (direction, consequence, walkable). Resumption is from chunks --pending and status, not conversation memory.
cards.measured: 51 chunks over 11 files all read and ingested (SESSION_STATE.md:53; ledger.json corpus_trail identified 11, read 11, unread 0 at ledger.json:593-594). ledger_events shows analyst decide-s2 batches accepted 39+39+38+38=154 and decide-s3 batches such as 57, 28, 14, 46 with 0 rejected. Reader work was run as two workflows because session limits interrupted 29 chunk reads (SESSION_STATE.md:53). No wall-clock, token or cost figure for construction was found.
cards.limits: One reader per chunk, so no inter-reader agreement can be measured (METHOD.md section 7, CL-10 not implemented). Readers and analysts are models; 6,000-character chunk size is a choice, not optimised. Extraction omissions unquantified: three skipped table headers alone imply at least 38 to 53 further edges (08-reapply/summary.md Limits). Construction cost was never measured, so cost-per-map-edge is unknown.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The pattern of fresh bounded readers writing records to files, validated by script and ingested by a single sequential writer, with chunk-hash identity and resumption from disk state, is directly reusable for any FixFlow bulk-extraction task (for example extracting invariants from docs). It also demonstrates that subagents can hand results back as files that a script validates, avoiding the long-report-through-orchestrator-context problem.

cards.name: Context packet query (cmap context/find/show/chain/gaps) as the recall mechanism
cards.what_it_is: The query surface that a fresh agent uses (QUICKSTART.md): status for freshness, find for lexical start suggestions (labelled S5, not evidence), context <start names or IDs> --budget N --depth D to get a paged packet by breadth-first expansion through section containment and incident edges, each record with slots, how each slot resolved, quote and file:lines; UNRESOLVED and GAP lines; FRONTIER lists unexpanded referents; MORE gives the next page; COVERAGE states read status of touched files; show path:start-end prints exact lines for citation; chain gives derived chains only over analyst-declared walkable kinds. Budget advice: start with 1-2 specific starts, keep --budget about 2,000-4,000 tokens. Packets default to L3 with analyst hops labelled; pages never split a sibling group.
cards.measured: None on delivered tokens or task quality. The only measured recall-like figure is extraction recall against the earlier V2 reading on the four identical pilot files: 0.523 exact and 0.588 exact-or-loose overall (09-operational/results/extraction-vs-v2.json, 'overall' block; per file: brief 0.538, decision-log 0.425, architecture 0.648, README 0.46). Static review (local-project-fit.md) found the packet budget is approximate: budget*4 characters (cmap.py:1158), sibling groups kept whole even if over the page (1173-1182), diagnostics appended after paging (1191-1215).
cards.limits: No comparison against routed reading ever ran (see A6-10). Static finding, not reproduced: the frontier may be drained before output because depth-exceeded referents are popped and skipped at cmap.py:1111-1114 and FRONTIER built at 1194, so omitted prerequisites may disappear. cmd_show builds root/path with no corpus containment check (cmap.py:1239-1257). No cumulative per-run budget; direct source reads are permitted by the worker prompt (harness/workspaces.py:23-31). Empty map answer does not prove absence.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: This is the closest thing in the lane to 'faster recall that minimises token use': ask by named start, get a size-bounded evidence packet with exact lines and an explicit frontier of what was not expanded. Transferable ideas: cite file:line quotes, always return unresolved/frontier lists, never present an empty answer as 'no dependency'. Unproven in token terms, so FixFlow should treat the numbers as unknown.

cards.name: Coverage ledger and freshness/refresh (self-maintaining map, partially)
cards.what_it_is: Per file version the ledger records read and unread chunk ranges, linked records by type, untyped relation cues, inert labels, dangling endpoints by subtype (named-not-specified, absent slot, external, identity not established, conflict), external targets, open candidates, and a corpus trail (identified/read/partly read/unread). Freshness: every query checks file hashes; records from a changed file are listed STALE and never served as evidence. refresh re-chunks a changed file, preserves records of chunks whose text hash is unchanged (ids kept, line spans remapped), supersedes records of changed or removed chunks (kept in file, excluded from answers), regenerates structural records, flags dependent S3 decisions needs_review until re-decided. Derived results are never cached as facts so nothing stale survives. Reading is explicitly not proof of complete extraction.
cards.measured: Map-wide totals at ledger.json:554-567: 4,053 dangling endpoints at L1 and L2 (3,109 named-not-specified, 441 identity-not-established, 459 absent slot, 44 external) and 3,673 at L3 after S3 decisions; 5 'claim without attested premise' flags. Refresh has only synthetic tests; the changed-source case C5 on a modified snapshot (S1-prime) was designed but not run (SESSION_STATE.md section 4 phase P9-6 not started).
cards.limits: File updates were out of scope for the design (D11) and added only as the experimental delta D-FRESH. Refresh has not been exercised on real edits. It is a manual command (cmap refresh), not an automatic watcher or hook; this is the nearest thing to 'self-evolving' and it is not self-updating. Large dangling counts show the map mostly records what the plan names but never specifies, which is noise unless filtered.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Chunk-text-hash identity plus supersede-not-delete plus STALE labelling at query time is a cheap way to keep a derived index honest as docs change. For FixFlow it would address CLAUDE.md's own 'keeping this file honest' problem (stale head number, stale paths) only if wired to a hook or CI; here it is manual.

cards.name: Pilot application and counts C1-C7 on four files
cards.what_it_is: Four frozen files (clinic-planning-brief, decision-log, architecture, technical-plan README) were read under design.v1 by the skeptic, and by an independent Explore-agent annotator with no project instructions whose chain was frozen: brief USER-04 ($8/month cap) to decision-log A11 to architecture '$8 quote' gate to README $7.79 total; frozen gap: itemised recurring hosting arithmetic required but never supplied. Counts C1-C7 plus later V0-V2 re-application under revised design and an L3 check.
cards.measured: design.v1: 427 attested edges (brief 98, decision log 116, architecture 137, README 76); 120 new labels, 0 with text-defined properties; 62 identity decisions needed, 563 dangling endpoints at L2; chain not reproduced at any level; gap partly reproduced (06-final/report.md C1-C7 table, lines 95-101). Revised design V2: 692 attested edges (481 without borderline records), 242 distinct labels (148 used once, 61%), 1,166 dangling endpoints at L2 (807), 785 distinct unresolved names (08-reapply/summary.md:32,39,54-55,59). L3 check: chain still not reproduced; gap PARTIAL (07-l3-check/verdict.md). Hop 1 (USER-04 to A11) connects only when 3-5 analyst decisions are made together; the two '$8' hops cannot be joined at any level (summary.md hop-1 table).
cards.limits: Four files only; single model readers so no agreement measure; frozen annotation is the only independent element and its annotator was a model. A 'mostly gaps' result is expected on a loosely linked corpus, not a success criterion. The design cannot express a link that exists only through a shared constraint value ('$8'), which is exactly the kind of cross-document dependency a human annotator saw first. Label-frequency tables do not establish analyst workload; no analyst time was measured (summary.md corrects an earlier claim).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A cautionary result: a strict attestation-only map recovered the human-visible dependency chain at none of the levels tested, and over half of labels were singletons. For FixFlow this argues against requiring text-cued relations; links through shared constants (for example a money limit or Alembic head number repeated across docs) need a different, explicitly labelled mechanism or a plain grep with a drift check.

cards.name: Skeptic round: 21 attacks, 12 accepted, 9 rejected
cards.what_it_is: One adversarial skeptic read the frozen design and applied it to the pilot, filing 21 counterexamples (K01-K21) over 10 groups A1-A10, each quote-checked against frozen files. The reasoner answered once: accept with applied diff, or reject citing exactly a G1 design step or a G2 constraint-block rule verbatim. 12 accepted, 15 elements revised, 3 rejected on G1 and 6 on G2. Three accepted points had already been self-flagged by the reasoner.
cards.measured: 21 attacks; 12 accept, 3 reject G1, 6 reject G2 (06-final/report.md:7 and section 6 table). 1,318 pilot-application items all quote-verified (report section 5). Model closed no counterexample and no unresolved claim (report.md line 3).
cards.limits: Skeptic and reasoner are both models of the same family; rejections rest on disputed readings of the design's own wording (K05, K14, K21). One response round then stop, so revised design (15 changed elements) was not re-applied until the later 08-reapply pass. A concession remains: a set or range citation like USER-03-14 can never reach a member at any level (K07).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Adversarial attacks forced to quote the passage and cite a verbatim rule, and rebuttals forced to cite a verbatim design step or rule, is a transferable review format that blocks hand-waving in both directions. It is a model-reading-model review, so it does not touch the missing human review (B17).

cards.name: Validation contract: map vs routed reading vs Graphify (frozen, never run)
cards.what_it_is: A pre-registered contract (contract.md, SHA c555d769; references 2240f5f0) written by the owner before any trial: 5 development cases C1-C5 (multi-step chain, missing support and the $8 negative case, misleading similar IDs, one repeated name with four referents, changed source), 3 arms (M map with persisted store and CLI; R routed reading via AGENTS.md, launcher and context-routing doc; G Graphify 0.9.81 default build), 2 runs per arm per case = 30 runs, fresh workers, budget 16,000 tokens of tool-result material (characters/4) and 30 tool calls per run, blinded evaluator scoring weighted obligations from sealed references (97 reference quotes verified by check_references.py), acceptance V1-V9, verdict rules viable/partially viable/not viable, and a rule that 'better' needs a 0.10 mean difference in the same direction in at least 4 of 5 cases.
cards.measured: None. The runs/ directory under 09-operational is empty; SESSION_STATE.md phase table (line 53 onward) lists P9-5 trials, P9-6 changed-source case, P9-7 evaluator, P9-8 repair, P9-9 verdict as 'not started'; no results file for these exists (only results/extraction-vs-v2.json). The map-arm acceptance thresholds, for example V1 mean obligation score at least 0.70 and V6 within 16,000 tokens and 30 calls (contract.md:79), were never tested.
cards.limits: Contract states its own limits: development cases not holdouts, 2 runs per arm shows variance only roughly, corpus would fit in one window, same model family for workers, readers and evaluator, AGENTS.md injected into every worker is a shared confound. Work moved on to the context-admission research on 2026-10-09 (A6-12) and this comparison was never completed.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The contract is a reusable template for A/B-testing any context aid against a baseline: frozen sealed references, equal budget, blinded scoring, mechanical citation check, and 'fewer tokens with missing prerequisites is not a win'. It should be run before building a map or graph for FixFlow, since in this repository it was never run.

cards.name: Trial harness: workspaces, transcript measurement, citation check, blind scoring
cards.what_it_is: Python scripts in 09-operational/harness: workspaces.py creates per-arm corpus workspaces and worker prompts; measure.py reads workflow agent-*.jsonl transcripts and computes material_chars/tokens (tool-result characters/4), tool_calls, peak_context_tokens, total_input and output tokens, baseline_context_tokens (first model call), and file paths named in tool inputs with an outside_workspace list; check_citations.py mechanically verifies cited quotes occur at cited lines; blind.py strips arm labels; compare_v2.py compared extraction to V2.
cards.measured: None from trials. Only compare_v2 output exists (extraction-vs-v2.json, A6-06). local-project-fit.md notes the harness is retrospective: it does not reject an excessive or outside-workspace read before it enters the model, and path strings in logged tool inputs are not a complete filesystem-access audit.
cards.limits: Token figures are characters/4 estimates, not provider tokenization; context peak is read from transcript usage fields. Isolation is audited after the fact. Written for the Codex/Claude workflow transcript format of that PC.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: measure.py-style post-hoc transcript accounting (material tokens, tool calls, peak context per agent) is a ready pattern for measuring FixFlow sub-agent cost per task from Claude Code transcripts; the same Windows PC and transcript layout apply. Needs adapting to Claude Code's jsonl schema.

cards.name: Candidate index (S5): similarity proposes, never decides
cards.what_it_is: A separate candidates.jsonl holds pairwise similarity, exact-ID-token and alias proposals each with method, score and disposition (open/accepted). No query level reads it; only find, the worklist (to propose analyst work) and a labelled --candidates section of a packet read it. A test deletes the file and checks that packets and gaps are byte-identical (test_levels_never_read_candidate_index). Similarity may prompt an analyst's S3 decision but never creates an S1 record.
cards.measured: 1,906 candidates in the S1 store (SESSION_STATE.md:53; wc -l candidates.jsonl); methods seen at the head of the file: token-jaccard score 0.5 and exact-id-token score 1.0. 93 open candidates for the brief file alone (ledger.json, brief 'open_candidates').
cards.limits: Candidates are lexical only (token Jaccard, ID token); no embeddings; precision not measured. Many are noise for short names ('Decision' matches 'Decision and reason' headers, 08-reapply/summary.md).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The separation rule is worth copying: a suggestion index that cannot enter evidence-bearing answers, enforced by a deletion test. It addresses retrieval-as-context contamination (R3) in any FixFlow recall tool.

cards.name: Graphify 0.9.81 comparator arm
cards.what_it_is: A third-party knowledge-graph tool (PyPI graphifyy 0.9.81) chosen as the comparator arm: isolated venv, default build, semantic extraction by host subagents in one chunk of 11 files, community labels by an agent, queries via graphify query/path/explain/affected, --update flow for changed source. No graphify install, hooks or settings changes were allowed.
cards.measured: Built graph over the 11-file snapshot: 92 nodes, 127 edges, 10 communities, health OK (SESSION_STATE.md section 4, row P9-4). Graph file lives in a git-ignored tmp/graphify/S1/graphify-out/graph.json which was not in this lane's scope and was not read. No query accuracy or token figure.
cards.limits: The graph is tiny (92 nodes for 167 KB) and no arm result exists. The checkpoint says community labelling and manifest steps were still running when the note was written. Whether graph.json is stored in SQLite was not checked.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: If FixFlow wants an off-the-shelf repository graph to test the owner's idea, Graphify is already evaluated for installability here but not for value; run it as arm G of a contract like A6-10 on FixFlow's docs before adopting anything.

cards.name: Context-admission research: the 700k to 800k refill loop
cards.what_it_is: A 2026-10-09 research package (10-context-admission-research) triggered by the owner's report that after a state file and new chat at about 700k tokens, two or three further runs refilled the window to about 800k through file reads, shell results, retrieval and startup injection. It judged a submitted proposal (submitted-proposal.txt, preserved unchanged) that claims claude-context-hooks stops the refill. Finding: saving state differs from controlling what later tools admit; no inspected default configuration bounds the refill. Unit of analysis is the maintained project across successive processes. Method: web discovery plus pinned-commit static source inspection; no installs, no upstream execution, no model trial. 15 discovery queries logged (root-search-ledger.json) and 19 more by the landscape lane.
cards.measured: 700k and 800k are USER-REPORTED, not reconstructed (report.md:19). Arithmetic growth witness: 400 distinct results of 8,000 ASCII bytes each is about 800k tokens under CCH's own characters/4 heuristic without spending its budget (claude-context-hooks-audit.md:43; report.md:23). Coverage: 23 pinned repositories in selected source audits (report.md:13), 19 in the landscape lane (github-landscape.md:5). verification.json: status pass; 226 baseline files unchanged, 87 local links, 42 root source hashes, 69 landscape committed-source hashes, 19 repo pins.
cards.limits: The README and report carry a SUPERSESSION notice dated 2026-10-09: the owner clarified the real requirement is automatic compression preserving task quality of about 800k in a 300-400k active context; the corpus-specific selection criteria and squeez-first recommendation are WITHDRAWN. Replaced by output/context-system-research (not read in this lane). Source reviews are static; no installed trial, no Opus 5.5 ultracode run. Peer review is a model review.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The decomposition of context growth into ingress routes (startup, native Read/Grep/Glob, shell stdout and stderr, retrieval/MCP, subagent returns) and the point that a per-call limit does not bound the sum of unique calls transfers to FixFlow's orchestrator-overflow problem (B04). The finding that a handoff file plus a new chat does not change what the next session admits is directly relevant.

cards.name: claude-context-hooks (CCH) and claude-context-manager: vendored hook set with a SQLite code-graph footer
cards.what_it_is: jimovonz/claude-context-hooks pinned at 089d6b08 (vendored under sources/claude-context-hooks) and its predecessor claude-context-manager pinned b0f84fd9 (sources/ccm, Linux-only, patched CLI). CCH registers nine PreToolUse matchers: denies native Read/Grep/Glob/WebFetch/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit and redirects to Bash helpers; wraps Bash stdout via cache-wrap.py (outputs over 8,000 bytes stored in a content-addressed cache and replaced by a stub; ccm-get.py retrieves slices); delta marker for repeated identical outputs; a shared passthrough budget file. Its Python files use sqlite3 to read a cairn-graph code-structure database (graph.db): cairn_graph_footer.py appends function-level callers/tests footers to code reads, intercept-agent.py redirects code-structure Explore agents to cairn-graph, ccm-get.py --symbol resolves symbol line spans from graph.db.
cards.measured: Audit finding (static, not executed): the passthrough budget is 25,000 estimated tokens in a five-hour renewable window kept in a user-level file (claude-context-hooks-audit.md:47); Bash stdout at most 8,000 bytes is not debited; stderr is unmetered; five literal broad regex spellings are charged but other broad patterns are not; a shell-shape loophole (helper command in one segment exempts the whole call); exit status 0 wrapping can hide inner failures. None of CCH's own savings claims were measured here.
cards.limits: CCH is third-party code vendored as evidence only (about 400 files), not a clinic-built library. Its graph is a CODE graph from the external cairn-graph tool (SQLite) and is useless for this markdown-heavy plan (audit notes Markdown not covered); hooks use fcntl (Unix), Windows and hook composition unqualified. Conclusion: shipped partial admission control, not proof it stops the refill.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: This is the only place in the lane where a SQLite graph exists. FixFlow is a code repository, so a cairn-graph style function-level callers/tests footer attached to reads of source could be relevant, and the stub-plus-retrieve cache for big outputs is a usable design. The bypass list (stderr, small outputs, slices, helper shell shapes) is a ready checklist for any FixFlow output-capping hook.

cards.name: Cairn (jimovonz/cairn): single-SQLite-file memory and proxy tool-schema paring
cards.what_it_is: A memory system for Claude Code pinned at a923ebe8: each response ends with a short structured block, a hook parses it out, stores it in one SQLite file and injects relevant entries into later sessions; five hook types; no extra LLM calls; no MCP. A proxy (cairn/proxy/server.py pare_tools) drops unused tool definitions while protecting names already used, and injects bootstrap context. PARE_TOOLS_ENABLED default on, PARE_CM_ENABLED default off; the spec docs/spec-context-paring.md describes future phases (stale-content demotion, consumed-result demotion) not shown as installed behaviour.
cards.measured: None measured. The audit reads README, spec, selected request/server/config code and a tool-paring test; graph extraction and retrieval quality were not audited or trialled.
cards.limits: Request path is fail-open (injection errors return original body); neither schema paring nor memory injection intercepts unique Read/Bash bytes; adds another injection route to budget; would merge attested records, analyst judgements and suggestions into undifferentiated memories unless constrained. This is the closest match to the owner's 'SQLite library with recall' as shipped software, yet it is third-party and not a repository graph.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Candidate comparator if FixFlow wants semantic cross-session memory in SQLite. Its tool-schema paring targets definition overhead, which matters for sessions with many MCP tools. Not adopted or tested in this repository.

cards.name: Headroom: proxy compression, read lifecycle, maturation
cards.what_it_is: headroomlabs-ai/headroom pinned 01d91948: proxy with cache and token modes; default 'coding' profile preserves cached prefix and protects reads from lossy compression; ReadLifecycle marks earlier reads stale after mutation or superseded after a later read covers them; opt-in beta read maturation replaces quiescent reads with CCR markers; session engine freezes prefix for cache consistency; context guard nudges client compaction at 90% of effective limit. Persistent CCR store is SQLite (config default sqlite:///headroom.db).
cards.measured: Maintainer claim of roughly 50% emergent savings under the default profile is recorded as the maintainer's estimate, not reproduced; the --budget flag is a daily USD budget, not a context cap. No restore test, resource benchmark, Windows trial or Opus 5.5 run was performed.
cards.limits: Fresh unique reads remain intact; does not bound an append-only sequence of unique reads; default profile keeps frozen prefix; context guard is a compaction pressure nudge it admits it cannot test in the client. Kept as comparator.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Read-lifecycle idea (demote reads made stale by an edit or superseded by a wider re-read) is a concrete, narrowly scoped mechanism that could cut repeated re-reading of the same FixFlow file within a session; needs a request-level proxy, which is a new moving part on the owner's PC.

cards.name: squeez (claudioemmanuel) native result rewriting: first trial subject, later withdrawn
cards.what_it_is: A Rust tool pinned b8d46531 that uses PostToolUse updatedToolOutput to rewrite native results, preserves the native Read result shape, deduplicates repeated Read/Skill/MCP results, adds default Read limit 300 lines and Grep 100 results only when the caller gives none, and offers squeez_retrieve to get originals. The 2026-10-09 report named it the preferred first trial subject for native result mediation, then the supersession notice withdrew that recommendation.
cards.measured: Release v1.48.18 observed. Defaults are line/result counts (Read 300, Grep 100), not token ceilings; no token savings measured here.
cards.limits: Explicit Read/Grep limits override defaults; unique Read bodies are dedup-only (not summarised); full retrieval returns the entire original; session dedup resets on a new session so the next run can re-read the whole corpus; no project-wide admission ledger; Bash has explicit bypass and risky-command passthrough.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The updatedToolOutput route (replacing native tool output in a PostToolUse hook, schema must match or original is used) is a supported Claude Code mechanism per the runtime audit (Claude Code v2.1.280 for Opus 5.5, v2.1.284 for Ultracode toggle); usable on the same Windows PC for FixFlow output capping, but parallel matching hooks run unordered.

cards.name: Other shipped context tools, each rejected as a complete remedy (context-mode, RTK, claude-mem, context-pruner, Firewall, Prismo, token-economy-kit and others)
cards.what_it_is: The github-landscape table covers 19 pinned repos. context-mode d573d8e: MCP execute/index/search, native Read/Grep advisory only, search guard rolling 60,000 ms window, taper after 3 calls, block after 8. RTK e4f0509: Bash command rewrites to compact filters. claude-mem fa8ab09: durable observations, 10,000-character startup injection, conditional whole-code-file Read gate. context-pruner 572c37d: a TLS-intercepting proxy that stubs older tool_use/result pairs per request but only for Chrome control tools by default. Context Firewall 5c0f3fc: MCP-only, RAM-only originals (30-minute TTL, 50 MiB / 200 entries). Prismo 89b3170: path-pattern denies and failing-command breaker. token-economy-kit d739fd2: denies oversized whole Reads including markdown, but any limit of at most 600 lines passes. Continuous-Claude-v3 d07ff4b: TLDR-backed Read denial for code only. claude-context-optimizer, context-forge, agent-squeeze, Clear Your Tools, Serena, Beads, GSD Core, claude-context-handoff and a token playbook were also assessed.
cards.measured: No efficacy measured. Per-repo release versions recorded for 12 products (for example RTK v0.51.0, claude-mem v13.35.0, context-mode v1.0.169, Serena v1.7.0, Beads v1.3.1, GSD Core v1.16.0). Source ledger hashes 69 committed source files at pinned commits (verification.json). Author-reported numbers noted but unverified: a token-playbook 39% overhead result, token-economy-kit file-corpus ceilings labelled 'removable ceilings, not average-session savings'.
cards.limits: Static review of selected files only; stars/forks kept as discovery metadata only; no installs, no trial in the owner's runtime. Individual per-tool verdicts are recorded as 'no inspected default establishes a complete bound'. Useful distinctions: durable memory is not an admission gate; handoff-only tools do not change what the next run admits; GSD-style fresh bounded workers reduce exposure only if the worker handback is size-governed.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A ready shortlist of mechanism classes with named bypasses. For FixFlow the most reusable components are fresh bounded workers with governed handbacks (answers B16/B04), RTK-style Bash output filtering and Read-gate-with-outline for oversized files, each needing a trial on the actual Claude Code version before relying on it.

cards.name: Integration and qualification proposal: project admission contract and ledger (superseded)
cards.what_it_is: A proposal for a controller around everything a Claude Code process can admit: separate resident input (per request) from admission (newly inserted bytes at ingress and repeated reintroduction), a persistent atomic project ledger with reset only after a named resident-release action, a boundary table (startup, native reads/searches, shell incl. stderr, retrieval/MCP, worker outputs, repeats and changes, cumulative control, failure, fidelity, observability), a finite longitudinal experiment with 3 arms (existing routed reading plus handoff; shipped candidate at defaults; candidate plus contract), three consecutive resumed processes per arm with two independent repetitions, and a mermaid data-flow of canonical sources to corpus map to selected packet to admission controller to bounded working set.
cards.measured: None. Numerical thresholds explicitly left unset: 'Do not treat the attachment's 8KB/25k numbers or the 16k/30-call development limits as universal optimal settings'.
cards.limits: Superseded notice at top: written for a scope misread; the current request is automatic compression preserving task quality. Not installed, not trialled. The contract insists on delivered-input observability; without it the resident ceiling is 'unverified'.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The ingress checklist and the resident-versus-admission accounting split are reusable for designing FixFlow's own session-size guard; the finite 3-resumes-by-2-repetitions test is a ready plan to test whether a context harness fixes the overflow at the orchestrator.

cards.name: Local-fit audit of the map's own tool and the independent peer review of the research
cards.what_it_is: local-project-fit.md audited the existing project against the admission requirement: map budget is approximate and per page, no cumulative allowance, worker prompt permits direct source reads, show has no corpus-containment check, probable frontier drop at cmap.py:1111-1194, state file stale (SESSION_STATE says METHOD.md and QUICKSTART.md pending while both exist). peer-review.md (a local subagent review) found 5 corrections PR-01..PR-05 (resident input must exclude response reserve; V6 is trace-evaluated, not an intake gate; define admission event; release mechanism; verdict terms tie to observability), all closed by 2026-10-09. Also nine proposed evaluation requirements for judging candidates.
cards.measured: Static line citations only: cmap.py:1158, 1173-1182, 1191-1215, 1111-1114, 1194, 1239-1257; workspaces.py:23-31. None reproduced; labelled 'code-reading observation, not a reproduced defect'.

cards.name: Superseding context-system research (pointer only)
cards.what_it_is: The README and report of the admission research are overwritten by a notice that the corpus-specific criteria and squeez-first conclusion are withdrawn and that the replacement is output/context-system-research. That folder's README names Claude Code Infinite 1.0.14 with MemTree as the closest shipped match (continuous request compression, background hierarchical memory, access to original transcript) and cites a maintainer-reported benchmark of Opus 5.5 with a 775k-token starting history compressed to about 420k with similar task scores. It also lists Virtual Context and Rolling Context, LCM, Distil, Jev and Scalpel.

cards.limits: That folder, docs/tasks/context-admission-research and its evidence-2026-10-10 subfolder were NOT read in this lane. Whether anything was installed afterwards is unknown from this lane.

cards.name: docs/repo-context-audit.md: one-day audit of a 61-file repository by parallel automated reviewers
cards.what_it_is: A 2026-10-01 audit that reviewed 61 starting files, produced 14 findings RC-01..RC-14 (7 stock/money/access spec findings; stale guidance such as RC-08/RC-09; proposed workflow amendments unimplemented RC-10; evaluation baseline ambiguity RC-11; team portability gap RC-12 because source-manifest.json stores cache paths outside the repo; hash-drift of older snapshots RC-13). Three parallel automated reviewers covered technical planning, research/provenance and coding workflow, reconciled by an integration review. Checks actually run are listed (JSON parse, 641-record CSV, local link targets, PDF hash match, 641 cached source members re-hashed with no failures, 6 PDFs rendered).
cards.measured: 61 files = 40 Markdown, 11 JSON, 6 PDFs, 1 CSV, 1 HTML, 1 Python, 1 DWG; 64 PDF pages across six PDFs; no Git repository in the folder at that date (docs/repo-context-audit.md, 'What this project currently contains' and 'Checks actually performed'). 59 unique project files matched their recorded hashes. No time or token cost recorded.
cards.limits: Automated review is 'not independent human or clinic acceptance'; line references in the audit drift as files change; DWG geometry never read. States that no local 3x/5x productivity result has been measured (RC-11).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The practice of a dated audit that separates hash-verified preservation from substantive review, and that records line-numbered findings plus a stale-guidance table, is a template for FixFlow's CLAUDE.md drift check. RC-12 (evidence stored outside the repo) maps to FixFlow's B11-style off-machine concerns.

cards.name: docs/technical-plan/reading-coverage.md: a hand-written reading-coverage ledger
cards.what_it_is: A file-by-file and page-by-page table recording that each required source was fully read before the architecture was saved, with order, coverage and access limits (truncated rows recovered in bounded follow-up reads; 41 PDF pages read, 8 also visually checked; a later 2026-10-21 efficiency/AI red-team review recorded a fresh full read). It is the manual predecessor of the map's coverage ledger. Verified once by a local script on 2026-09-30: 10 plan Markdown files, 41 coverage rows, USER-01-14, 13 slices, 20 tests T01-T20, 14 decisions, 15 questions, local links and code fences.
cards.measured: Counts above come from the file's own text; Section 'Page-by-page coverage' begins at line 37 and the verification record at line 97. No measure of whether coverage tables reduced rework.
cards.limits: Hand-maintained, so it drifts: the file prefixes later review notes above the original September record and admits a stale D: root and an older output copy. Records that something was read, not that it was understood.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A read-coverage table (what was read in full, what only by sampling, with limits) attached to an architecture or audit deliverable is a cheap honesty device against B12 overstated reports; FixFlow could script it from agent transcripts instead of hand writing it.

cards.name: Recorded failures in the map programme: session limits, resume replay, fabricated-looking drift, long-path clone
cards.what_it_is: Documented incidents: (1) account session limits interrupted lane agents six times (SESSION_STATE.md section 5) and six of eight lanes failed in run 1; (2) a resumed workflow replayed nothing because its first agent() call had failed, so every later call ran live and re-run agents edited prior files; edits were recovered from transcripts and reversed, byte sizes and validator counts re-matched; the rule 'never resume a workflow whose first agent() call failed; launch a fresh run' was written into SESSION_STATE; (3) a Graphify extraction agent wrote its file before its final reply was cut off; (4) the reducer's parallel fetch recorded a captcha page as text, leaving 11 quotes unverified until fixed (interstitials now treated as fetch errors, one sequential retry); (5) cloning the predecessor into its long repository name hit the Windows long-path limit and needed git core.longpaths=true; (6) an early reading of 'costs measured' for P9-3 was never filled; (7) earlier summary claims later withdrawn by the owner's reviews (for example 'identity not vocabulary is the scaling cost' withdrawn in 08-reapply/summary.md; 25 of 37 corrected to 27 in report.md C6).
cards.measured: Counts: 133 queries of aborted agents recovered from transcripts into 01-lanes/*.queries.recovered.txt (run.md G1 row); 4 quotes never verified (ECO source); 11 quotes initially unverified due to captcha (run.md incident 4). Six interruptions (SESSION_STATE.md section 5).
cards.limits: Recovery was by the orchestrator re-deriving state from transcripts and byte sizes; no automatic resume. Nothing here reduces dependence on the owner's usage limit; it only records how to resume. SESSION_STATE.md is a model-written checkpoint that was already stale within hours (see A6-21).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Concrete lessons: write role outputs to files so an interrupted agent leaves evidence; checkpoint-by-state-file plus idempotent resume from disk (chunks --pending); never trust a resume whose first call failed; treat model-authored summaries as claims to re-verify (this repository's own owner reviews corrected the model's counts three times).
