result.notes:
DIRECT ANSWER TO THE OWNER'S RECOLLECTION. (1) 'A SQLite graph-based library for a self-evolving repository': nothing in this lane matches literally. The clinic's own graph is the corpus map (A6-03, A6-04): a typed-edge graph of the PLAN documents (attested relations between named referents with exact quoted spans, gaps, coverage), stored as JSON-lines files under output/corpus-map-justification/09-operational/store/S1, driven by one Python CLI (tools/cmap.py). It was never put into SQLite, and it is not a graph of code. The only SQLite graphs here are third-party code the research inspected and vendored as evidence: claude-context-hooks reads a cairn-graph code-structure graph.db (function callers/tests footers, symbol lookup) and jimovonz/cairn keeps memory in one SQLite file; headroom has a SQLite CCR store (A6-15, A6-16, A6-17). The vendored claude-context-hooks hook file hooks/lib/cairn_graph_footer.py is very likely the 'one vendored hook file' the main scout found. 'Cairn' = jimovonz/cairn (a memory+graph tool by a GitHub user), not a clinic component. 'Self-evolving': the closest real mechanism is refresh with chunk-hash identity, supersede-not-delete and STALE labelling (A6-07), but it is a manual command, only synthetic-tested and never run on a real edit. (2) 'Faster recall that minimises token use': the corpus-map context packet (A6-06) is the intended mechanism (size-budgeted, exact-span evidence packets with frontier and gaps; QUICKSTART says use budget 2,000-4,000 tokens) but no measurement of tokens or quality against reading the files ever happened: the validation contract (A6-10) that would measure it was frozen and never run, and the plan corpus (about 41.7k tokens) is small enough to read whole. The only quantitative recall-like figure is extraction recall against a prior reading: 0.523 exact, 0.588 loose. The later context-admission research (A6-14 to A6-20) addresses a different problem (token growth to 800k in a session) by surveying shipped tools; its recommendation was withdrawn on 2026-10-09 and superseded by output/context-system-research (not read here).

CAUTIONS. All numbers above are quoted as read; no figure was invented or rounded except where stated 'about'. Several are corrected by the owner's own reviews inside the files, so later correction notes (report.md C6, summary.md withdrawn claim) govern. Evidence quality for the programme overall is that every reader, analyst, verifier, skeptic, evaluator and reviewer is a model; the only independent human elements are the owner's rulings and review memos recorded in SESSION_STATE and unresolved.md. For FixFlow the strongest transferable items are: quote-verifying scripts and transcript audits against overstated reports (A6-02, A6-11), the S1-S6 status discipline and the rule that similarity never becomes evidence (A6-03, A6-12), chunk-hash freshness with supersede-not-delete (A6-07), the pre-registered A/B contract template (A6-10), the ingress-by-ingress admission checklist with named bypasses (A6-14, A6-15, A6-20) and the recorded resume/session-limit failures (A6-25). The strongest negative lesson is that a large amount of design and research effort (8-lane harvest, 99-rule design, 21-attack skeptic round, 3 re-application passes, a 51-chunk store) preceded any measurement of whether the map helps an agent, and the decisive trial was never run.

result.lane: A7 coding-workflow and measurement research (docs/agentic-coding, tools/coding_workflow.py, output/coding-workflow, workflow/measurement/red-team/lean-workflow task folders, efficiency red-team review)

cards.name: task.md as single current-state owner; plan/review/handoff/context as projections
cards.what_it_is: docs/tasks/<id>/task.md is the one current-state index, kept by one integrating implementer. plan.md owns design, review.md findings; handoff, context packet and checkpoint JSON are timestamped projections that cannot overrule a newer task index. Code and performed checks govern facts; a ticked box proves nothing. Resolved errors are retired from the active summary with a link; full logs stay outside the packet.
cards.measured: none. Only a count: 37 task folders under docs/tasks. No resume time, rediscovery or conflict rate was measured.
cards.limits: Does not fix B13: it concentrates edits in one owner, so it encodes the single-writer pattern rather than removing it. Hashes cannot show the index is true. Nothing tests that agents follow the rule. Resume after a halt still needs someone to start a session.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The state/design/evidence/projection split and 'retire resolved errors, keep concise unresolved ones' transfer to FixFlow task and handoff records. Reconsider the single-owner rule for B04/B13 rather than copying it.

cards.name: Checkpoint + resume freshness check (hash of declared dependencies)
cards.what_it_is: tools/coding_workflow.py (378 lines, stdlib only) has doctor, verify, checkpoint, resume, validate-run and pilot subcommands. checkpoint hashes (SHA-256) the task.md, a context packet and chosen source files into a new JSON; resume re-hashes them and reports changed or deleted dependencies. Unrelated file changes do not invalidate. Output files are exclusive-create under docs/tasks or output/coding-workflow, never overwritten.
cards.measured: output/coding-workflow/WF-01/pilot.json: freshCheckpointAccepted true, unrelatedChangeAccepted true, staleDependencyRejected true, 24 reader subprocess calls, 6 packet-preparation reads. 29 behaviour tests pass (docs/tasks/workflow-implementation/task.md:27). Checkpoints were refreshed repeatedly (red-team projection reached checkpoint 011, docs/tasks/documentation-red-team/task.md:42).
cards.limits: Whole-file granularity: a changed dependency forces re-inspection of the whole file (lean task :31). Hash equality proves unchanged bytes, not truth or completeness. The pilot's fresh reader is a Python subprocess, not an LLM session (pilot.json limits). Caller picks dependencies by hand. Does not resume a halted session by itself (B03).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Cheap, no-dependency stale-handoff detector. FixFlow could checkpoint the board and key docs a session relied on, and on resume list only the changed ones. Useful against context overflow/summarisation losses (B04) and stale AGENTS.md or context-map parts (B13).

cards.name: Compact context packet versus baseline routing (byte-level pilot)
cards.what_it_is: Six predeclared synthetic cases (D01-D06: receipt, count, supplier settlement, restricted payroll, interrupted work, freshness) with 4 required facts each. Deterministic readers received a baseline packet and a compact projection twice. Treatment bytes include packet preparation reads. Each case had to keep every fact and reject a deliberately removed fact.
cards.measured: pilot.json:73-76 deliveredPayloadBytes baseline 10010, treatment 7947 (UTF-8 bytes, treatment including preparation). Per case baseline/treatment bytes: D01 1626/1261, D02 1602/1225, D03 1634/1273, D04 1754/1453, D05 1692/1360, D06 1702/1375. By my own division treatment is about 20.6 percent smaller; the file states no ratio. All 24 facts retained, lost-fact rejection true in every case. elapsedSeconds 0.737. inputTokens, providerCostUsd, humanProductivity are null.
cards.limits: Constructed fixtures, deterministic extraction; not model-generated context and not a distribution of real retrievals. Bytes are not tokens. No LLM was used. The docs explicitly refuse any 3x/5x claim (pilot.json limits). This is the repo's closest 'faster recall / fewer tokens' item, and it is a hand-built markdown projection, not a database or graph.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Method transfers: freeze required facts before building a compact packet, count bytes at the delivery boundary including preparation, and require a deliberate lost-fact to be rejected. The ~20% figure is not evidence for FixFlow.

cards.name: verify command + pre-commit hook + Git foundations
cards.what_it_is: verify checks Markdown links and fences, JSON parse, two provenance PDF hashes, instruction-presence contracts and runs the workflow unittest suite. A local pre-commit hook (tools/git-hooks/pre-commit) execs the same verify with an interpreter from clinicWorkflow.python. tools/verify_git_foundations.py proves reproduction from a committed HEAD in a disposable clone, including blocked bad commits. Ignore policy excludes secrets, caches and temp copies.
cards.measured: workflow-rollout/task.md:32 quotes commit 5ff2fae; 227 tracked files byte-identical to committed blobs; 29 workflow tests pass; all ten Git validations pass; valid commit accepted, broken-link and missing/invalid-interpreter commits rejected with HEAD unchanged. Last change to tools/coding_workflow.py in git history is e74fee5 (baseline), so none of the RT repairs landed.
cards.limits: Hook checks the working tree, not the staged bytes (RT-04), is bypassable, and treats 'Ran N tests' as success so an all-skipped suite passes (RT-01; tools/coding_workflow.py:354). Same machine only. No remote was created or contacted (B11 untouched). Not the application gate: since 3 Nov the app has scripts/check.py, which the hook does not run.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The disposable-clone reproduction probe and the idea of testing the gate with injected failures transfer. Copy the lesson, not the code: a gate must fail on skipped, unrun or empty suites. FixFlow's CI already has three jobs; the transferable item is negative controls for each gate.

cards.name: Application check later counts skips as failure and proves every test ran once
cards.what_it_is: The clinic application check (scripts/check.py) runs seven steps and a two-pass pytest: a parallel pass (xdist, 6 workers, one test DB per worker) and a single-process pass for tests marked serial, 'proving every test ran exactly once, with skipped, xfailed or xpassed tests counted as failure'. A machine-wide file lock caps concurrent full test runs. This independently fixes in the app the defect RT-01 records in the workflow tool.
where: docs/tasks/clinic-build/task.md:11 (S00 gate: 'root check 7/7 with 220 tests, 0 skipped')
cards.measured: command-catalogue.md:34: a full run takes about five minutes on the owner's PC; at most two full runs at a time, one per checkout, bounded wait 45 minutes; second slot only while 8 GiB is available. clinic-build/task.md:11: 220 tests, 0 skipped at the S00 gate. Details are another lane's territory.
cards.limits: Cited here only because the A7 documents record it; the mechanism itself was not read in scripts/check.py. Queueing (B07) and the 8 GiB rule are mitigations, not a fix.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Skip/xfail/xpass-as-failure and 'each test ran exactly once' are cheap guards against green-but-empty checks (B12). The machine-wide lock and memory-gated second slot address B05/B07/B08.

cards.name: WF-02 real-agent trial: with versus without compact packet + stale checkpoint
cards.what_it_is: Two isolated clones from base commit e74fee5; baseline got current task/source records, treatment additionally a compact packet and a deliberately stale checkpoint. Both repaired a broken synthetic adapter runner, then took two undisclosed follow-up requirements while keeping their own code. Evaluator oracle was frozen before dispatch (sha256 0a12cb31...). Two other-implementer static reviews followed.
cards.measured: trial-summary-final.json: 6 accepted stages, 38 scenario check executions, 9 unique final cases per condition (passed 4, 6, 9 in each), 2 usage-interrupted dispatches, 8 schema-valid run records. elapsed_minutes (line 32): phase0 8.587 baseline vs 8.588 treatment; phase1 193.134 vs 194.705 (includes the usage-limit wait); phase2 6.182 vs 6.183. providerTokens, allWorkerCostUsd, humanActiveMinutes, productivityRatio, contextEfficiencyRatio all null. Decision recorded: both met the same acceptance; no measured gain justifies more mandatory process.
cards.limits: One small synthetic task per condition, not randomized, 38 executions are not 38 tasks. Follow-ups reused worker conversations. Fresh workers resumed seeded work, not their own interrupted work. Review is automated static, no human. Tokens, cost and human effort unknown. Shows no benefit of the packet. Records the Codex-era harness, not Claude Code.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Transferable design: frozen external oracle before dispatch, identical broken start, two undisclosed follow-ups, retain every attempt. The null result (identical acceptance, near-identical time) is itself a finding: on small tasks a compact packet gave no measurable speed advantage.

cards.name: Usage-limit interruption recorded in WF-02
cards.what_it_is: The phase-1 dispatch for both conditions was stopped by the account usage limit before implementation; work resumed only after the user typed 'continue where you left off'. The interruption is kept in latency and attempt records and not hidden as compute.
cards.measured: usage-interruption json: startedAtUtc 2026-10-01T18:55:40.811730, workerFailureObservedAtUtc 22:01:53, resume dispatch 22:02:00 (about 3h06m); summary calls it 'roughly three-hour'. Phase-1 elapsed was 193.1 and 194.7 minutes (run-*-phase-1.json line 32).
cards.limits: Only recorded and labelled as an environment cause (WF-04 design says an outage and lost telemetry are different phenomena). No mitigation, scheduler or auto-resume was built or evaluated. B03's three-day stall is not addressed.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Evidence that the same usage-limit stop recurred early in the testbed. Record the wait separately from active work, and keep a state record complete enough that resume needs only one nudge. Nothing here removes the human trigger.

cards.name: Evaluation protocol: metric definitions, baseline/treatment rules, 3x arithmetic
cards.what_it_is: Primary measure is accepted tasks per active human engineering hour; elapsed time, agent minutes, cost, first-attempt acceptance, escaped defects and maintainability reported separately. Freeze the actual current baseline, change one mechanism at a time, isolated checkouts, randomised order, held-out acceptance, all assigned attempts kept. Candidate tasks E01-E16; JSON run schema plus validate-run. Includes a bound: removing a 20 percent avoidable share gives at most 1.25x.
cards.measured: none. evaluation-plan.md:95 gives the 1.25x bound as illustrative arithmetic; :93 a hypothetical 90 to 30 minute example, labelled not a result. Schema and validator exist; WF-02 produced 8 schema-valid records with null telemetry.
cards.limits: No 3x/5x claim established anywhere. Validator accepts defects (RT-03, RT-06): elapsed 1000 minutes off, human hours with null minutes (measurement-research.md:36-42). Needs human effort and token telemetry nobody collected.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The four-way split (quality, context, productivity, cost) and the Amdahl-style bound are reusable to decide where a harness could possibly pay off: if only X percent of effort is avoidable, the ceiling is 1/(1-X). Useful to size bottlenecks B01 and B04 before building anything.

cards.name: Measurement research WF-03: no collector exists; what is actually measured
cards.what_it_is: Audit and research showing the repository has a record validator and trial exports but no system that captures resources per task, reconciles workers and computes comparisons. Contains three in-memory probes of validator defects, a capability probe of the Codex CLI (--json, usage schemas) and evidence on METR and SPACE/DORA style measurement.
cards.measured: measurement-research.md:21: at base d3f72e3 eight active exports, all with null provider tokens, human effort, worker runtime, cost, payload size, resume duration, rework, escaped defects; :36-40 three validator probes; :56 METR early-2025 RCT, 16 developers, 246 issues, AI access increased completion time 19 percent (external study, not local).
cards.limits: Proposal only. All eight exports use zero for repeated reads without a collector (line 42), so those zeros are not evidence. Live per-worker event availability in the desktop route was not established.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Principal lesson: an unmeasured workflow cannot be called improved. For FixFlow, log per-session wall time, usage and rework from day one in a small append-only file; the Claude Code transcripts may expose usage, which was Codex-specific here.

cards.name: Measurement system design: ledger, identities, optional SQLite index
cards.what_it_is: Proposed pipeline: frozen condition manifest, adapters (owned CLI JSONL, app-server events, OTel, versioned rollout fallback), normalisation/reconciliation into per-run per-worker JSONL streams with sealed hash manifests, then coverage and claim-eligibility checks. Identity hierarchy experiment, task, stage, attempt, worker, call, artifact, human interval. States 'A rebuildable SQLite index is optional after demonstrated query needs; it must not become the only durable evidence'.
cards.measured: none
cards.limits: Nothing built. AGENTS.md:22 records the owner's decision that measurement research is low priority and M00/H00 must not start unless asked. The SQLite index is for measurement observations, not for code recall, and is explicitly optional.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: If FixFlow wants measurement, copy the append-only JSONL-plus-hash-manifest pattern and per-person interval union. This is the only SQLite mention in the lane, and it is not a graph or recall store.

cards.name: WF-04 expansion: standards, native-tool qualification, G0-G8 gates
cards.what_it_is: Three research agents plus root produced reports on methods and standards (GQM, ISO 15939 etc.), coding-quality evaluators and tool integration, plus qualification gates for the measurement system itself. Decisions D01-D12 changed the earlier plan: qualify maintained tools (Promptfoo native Codex providers, Langfuse/Phoenix adapters) before writing a runner, compare assigned not successful tasks, require independent oracles, prove holdout inaccessibility.
cards.measured: task.md:26: registers hold 27 methods, 23 coding-quality and 44 tool source groups. tools-and-integration.md:52-58 lists source-visible traps in Promptfoo 0.123.1: absent cache usage defaults to 0, replay reports cost 0, empty assertion list passes with score 1 ('No assertions'), judge may call another provider by default.
cards.limits: No tool was installed or run. No agent output was compared with a human. Several traps (no-assertion pass, defaults to zero) are statements read from source, not reproduced.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: G0-G8 and the 'green can mean nothing was checked' trap list are a checklist to audit FixFlow's own gates (jest, pytest, expo export): zero tests, skipped, defaulted cost fields. Directly relevant to B12 and B17.

cards.name: Measurement implementation plan H00/M00-M06
cards.what_it_is: Seven bounded slices: H00 maintained-tool fit; M00 identity/policy/contracts; M01 offline normalisation; M02 command-result and human-interval acquisition; M03 live client calibration; M04 offline reports; M05 feasibility on real tasks; M06 held-out confirmation. First task fixed on 5 Oct as M00 plus one H00 offline fit, then stop.
cards.measured: none
cards.limits: Not started; owner decision on 1 Nov 2026 (AGENTS.md:22) says do not start unless asked. RT-03 and RT-06 must be fixed for results to be trusted.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Cautionary example of research scope outgrowing use: three research rounds produced zero collectors. If FixFlow wants measurement, build M00-style contracts only for the one decision they inform.

cards.name: Red-team findings RT-01..RT-09 on the workflow tools
cards.what_it_is: A 3 Oct review (baseline 27febf9, 262 files, nine perspectives) found nine defects in the gates themselves: all-skipped suite passes, python -O removes oracle asserts, accepted plus critical failure in one record, hook checks working tree not commit, git probes depend on ambient config, unknown repeated-read count cannot be represented, launcher claims no Git, ambiguous first-task scope, valid Windows links reported missing in deep paths. Each has reproduction, correction and closure condition.
cards.measured: defects.md:3: 3 P1, 5 P2, 1 P3; eight OPEN, RT-08 closed by document reconciliation. RT-01 reproduction: 29 tests, 'OK (skipped=29)', verify exit 0 (defects.md:11). RT-02: the faulty artifact exits 2 normally and 0 under python -O with all nine cases passing (:23). Coverage 262 files, 228 in scope, 77 Markdown read (task.md:58). Git log: coding_workflow.py unchanged since e74fee5; task last committed in 8a1ce75.
cards.limits: No code repair was made; the clinic build moved to application slices and RT-01 stayed 'next action'. Review was automated, not independent human. Severity concerns workflow evidence, not deployed clinic failure.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The defect shapes (vacuous success, optimisation flags disabling asserts, validator accepting contradictory records, hooks checking different bytes than the commit) are a ready red-team checklist for FixFlow's own hooks and check scripts.

cards.name: Execution plan for repairs and the two-audience completion criterion
cards.what_it_is: A 5 Oct plan orders repairs RT-01, RT-02, RT-03, RT-09, RT-05, RT-04 with real dependencies, and requires each substantial task to deliver both a focused agent packet and a human explanation (goal, affected flow, choice, before/after, checks, next action). One integrating implementer per repair; helpers get bounded questions or disjoint files and return result, evidence, uncertainty, remaining action.
cards.measured: none. Planning verification: 29 tests, 325-file baseline, three read-only peer reviews (task.md:52).
cards.limits: Plan was ready but never executed for RT-01 (see A7-13). The human view adds maintenance cost, which the docs say is unmeasured. Automatic sync not built.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The 'bounded worker handback' format (result, evidence, uncertainty, remaining action) and the second audience (owner-readable explanation with diagrams) address B14 (owner cannot see progress) at low cost.

cards.name: Lean-workflow reassessment: nine dispositions and external evidence on instruction files
cards.what_it_is: The owner pasted a minimal-surface proposal (one short instruction file, no docs, 8 files/400 lines rejection, 120-word PR cap, hook ban on new Markdown, memory as only store). Task table disposes each row: keep root authority, reject no-docs, treat size triggers as review triggers not gates, reject hook allowlist. Also checked primary sources on context files and hooks.
cards.measured: task.md:14: root AGENTS.md 28 lines, 6,709 bytes at baseline. External figures quoted there: context files raised inference cost by over 20 percent on average (Gloaguen, :57); 124 PR tasks ten repos, AGENTS.md lowered median runtime/output tokens, input tokens not (Lulla, :59); 17 tasks, 288 runs, no detectable correctness benefit (Khatri, :60). Not local measurements.
cards.limits: No hook, memory or instruction change adopted; proposed comparison never run. Studies are small or differently scoped. Docs say line caps do not measure context cost.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Useful for CLAUDE.md hygiene: audit redundancy, keep one owner per rule, treat auto-loaded size and delivered task context as separate levers, and verify what actually loaded. Note CLAUDE.md here is already large; the evidence supports measuring before trimming.

cards.name: Source adoption audit of the four reference repos (12-factor, ACE, GenSX example, enterprise starter)
cards.what_it_is: Source-first audit with findings A01-A11 and a W01-W06 amendment plan. Adopted narrowly: code-shape block, boundary checks for adapters, fail-before/pass-after for bug fixes, single task state owner, error retirement, command evidence with effects/scope, configuration-to-consumer checks, iterative-change trajectory. Explicitly not adopted: installing runtimes, HumanLayer, GenSX, webhooks, Kubernetes, vector database or an orchestrator.
cards.measured: source-adoption-audit.md:17,26: pins checked against 641-file inventory; no upstream tests run. 12-factor audit statuses: factors F02 and F05 Partial, F03/F08/F09 full core with partial lifecycle details, F13 captured but partially specified (lines 62-73). GenSX: correction A10 (overstated mutation claim) and new finding A11 (denial feedback dropped by the real example).
cards.limits: Documents-only; the 'adopted' items are only partly exercised (WF-01 implemented W02/W03/W05, not enforcement). The sources are one author lineage, not independent replications (upstream README:22-24). PR #184/#186 already cover Horthy/BAML ideas, so only the clinic's local disposition is recorded here.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The adopt/reject split is the useful part: concrete additions (code shape, boundary trace caller to effect to result to consumer, config option to consumer, fail-before/pass-after test) are small fields, not frameworks. The 'do not install runtimes' stance matches FixFlow's no-orchestrator constraint.

cards.name: Four-repository full-tree reassessment (2026-10-04)
cards.what_it_is: Complete-tree review of humanlayer/humanlayer, agentcontrolplane, 12-factor-agents and advanced-context-engineering with per-file ledgers. Conclusions: directory-scoped instruction files are legitimate but one authority per rule; keep the lightweight workflow as a candidate to test; measurement acquisition semantics are hazardous (latest-message token overwrite, subagents excluded, guessed usage); comparison needs the actual baseline, one-addition treatment and all attempts.
cards.measured: README:29-36: HumanLayer 794, ACP 289, 12-factor 499, ACE 76 tracked files = 1,658; task.md:38: all 1,658 rehashed, zero missing or mismatched. HumanLayer CLAUDE.md nine paths, AGENTS.md zero (:62).
cards.limits: Inventory and hash match is not reading; no upstream code or test was run; both-client instruction-loading qualification unperformed (:107-112). Per-file reports not read in this lane (only README).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Already compiled in FixFlow PRs #184/#186; only the cross-checks matter: do not equate a stored token field with spend, and verify instruction loading in the actual client.

cards.name: Perplexity to Claude to Codex bridge assessment and ROI formula
cards.what_it_is: Assessment of a pasted three-tool routine: external research note, Claude plans/implements, Codex reviews read-only, human disposes, Claude repairs, checks rerun. Recommended as a candidate with amendments: research only for a material external unknown, freeze decision basis but allow versioned reopening, review a stable candidate, add a final repair-and-recheck leg, keep review gate off, risk not size to decide planning.
cards.measured: workflow-bridge-assessment.md:79: external cross-model study cited, 91.4 vs 82.8 percent on 116 single-file Python tasks (not local). :184-198: break-even n x (s - o) - F, illustrative F=120, o=12, s=5/25/60 minutes (explicitly not measurements); :200 bound 1.25x at 20 percent avoidable effort.
cards.limits: Never trialled. Review wait and triage cost unmeasured. A different model can share the writer's assumptions; docs require evidence not agreement. Human adjudication remains the bottleneck.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Addresses B01 and B17 conceptually: findings need trigger, violated requirement, affected path, consequence and reproduction; review is bound to a frozen candidate, and the final correction is re-verified. The break-even formula n(s-o)-F is a cheap way to judge any new harness component.

cards.name: Effectiveness review F01-F10: metric meaning, context freshness, early operating proof
cards.what_it_is: Secondary review of the plan and workflow. Product-side P1/P2 gaps (stock eligibility by command, period close against concurrent posting, upload safety, dependency edges, early operating proof) plus workflow gaps (3x measures productivity not quality; code-shape block; context freshness test; freeze baseline; separate cost). Proposes four separate measures and an extra run-record field list.
cards.measured: none. effectiveness-review.md:139: illustrative hosting $7.79 against an $8 cap (planning arithmetic).
cards.limits: Proposals only; the document says it is a secondary review and findings are not observed defects. F05 asks for a disposable synthetic deployment after S03 with backup, clean restore and a migration, restore from material independent of the app disk; whether that was done is outside this lane (S11 operations, another lane).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: F05 is the same remedy as B02 and B19: walk a clean install and restore end to end early, not at the end. F08 (test resumption and freshness) and F09 (freeze actual baseline) are direct measurement-design rules.

cards.name: Efficiency and AI red-team review of the clinic guide (ER-01..ER-08)
cards.what_it_is: 21 Oct 2026 review of the clinic's visual guide: single Django app retained; restore changes what safe retry means; count barrier cannot stop physical movement; AI failure must not delay core work; guide statements that differ from sources; combined entry journeys; duplicate work with existing system; efficiency claims need comparable evidence; recovery tolerance unproven. Proposes A/B/C comparison of ordinary forms, simplified forms and optional AI.
cards.measured: none. efficiency-ai-red-team-review.md:134 quotes existing proposed gates (posting p95 below 1 second, list/report below 2 seconds, peak memory below 3.2 GB in a 4 GB envelope, offsite backup within an hour). :156 records two lead-side recovery notes: combined-output truncation recovered with smaller reads, one console encoding failure corrected.
cards.limits: Concerns the product (clinic), not the build harness. Two parallel AI reviewers, not human validation; no application existed to benchmark. Low direct transfer to FixFlow; the clinic app is Django, not FastAPI.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Only the process lessons: bring a small performance and recovery proof into early slices (ER-07, same as B19/B20), measure p95 under the documented workload with each optional component off/slow/failed, and keep AI calls outside transactions with bounded retries.

cards.name: Evidence-status vocabulary and 'automated is not human' labelling
cards.what_it_is: Records distinguish REPORTED/OBSERVED/DOCUMENTED/INFERRED/PROPOSED/UNKNOWN, passed vs failed vs unrun, unknown (null) vs zero, automated review vs independent human review, hash freshness vs truth. Every task states what its checks do not establish.
cards.measured: none
cards.limits: It is a convention; no check enforces it beyond schema nullability. It produced very long limit paragraphs (for example tasks/documentation-red-team/task.md:42 is one dense paragraph with eight amendments), adding reading cost and arguably feeding B13 doc staleness.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A short report template with 'Checked / Not checked / Unknown' columns would reduce B12 (reports overstating) cheaply. Keep the vocabulary small.

cards.name: Before/after file manifests and preservation comparisons per task
cards.what_it_is: Each workflow task writes a hash manifest of all tracked/unignored files before editing and a preservation comparison after, showing only intended files changed and sources/archives untouched. Also source-reconciliation passes (for example 1,658 upstream files rehashed).
cards.measured: Examples: 247 baseline files all accounted for, only six declared documents changed (expansion task.md:38); 23 protected source paths unchanged (workflow-rollout task.md:36). No timing cost recorded.
cards.limits: Catches unintended change, not wrong change. Adds ceremony per task. Git diff --stat provides most of it where a repo already exists.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: In a Git repo, a pre-task `git diff --stat` or tree hash recorded in the task gives the same guard; for parallel sessions (B15) it makes 'what did this session touch' auditable.

cards.name: Bounded delegation brief and parallel research agents writing owned files
cards.what_it_is: Delegation brief template (question, source scope, ownership read-only or disjoint files, return form, stop condition). WF-04 used three research agents each owning one report file; lean-workflow research used three read-only subagents with a ceiling of four workers; root integrates and cross-checks, not by vote.
cards.measured: none (lean task:120: 'Four workers were the available concurrency ceiling; extra worker count is not evidence of better results').
cards.limits: Agents there wrote report files directly, so it does not show a way round B16 (subagents cannot write files in the FixFlow Claude Code setup). Root still reads and checks the key conclusions, so the serial gate (B04) remains. Cost of delegation not measured.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Report-to-owned-file with short handback could reduce orchestrator context load if FixFlow subagents can be given a writable path; otherwise the brief format still helps. Needs verification in the FixFlow tool setup.

cards.name: Windows and environment failures recorded in the workflow
cards.what_it_is: Concrete environmental failures logged: valid links reported missing when parent segments push a Windows path over the limit (RT-09); Python application-execution alias is not Python; Windows input framing and executable-hook metadata issues in WF-02; stale launcher claiming no Git (RT-07) and stale root path after the OneDrive copy vanished; agents working on a partial D: copy and wrongly concluding plans were missing; ZIP-based inventory used to avoid long-path scan omissions; one console encoding failure.
cards.measured: none (qualitative records; for example verification.md:11 names 641 inventory entries built from ZIPs).
cards.limits: Not about the two PC crashes (B05) or Docker (B06/B09/B10): nothing in this lane touches memory, shutdowns or containers.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: State the working root and base revision in every launcher and handoff and verify it first (local-audit.md:42). Treat path length and shell quirks on Windows as test cases for any link or path checker.

cards.name: Owner's recollection test: SQLite graph library and faster recall in this lane
cards.what_it_is: Search result, not a mechanism: nothing in the A7 documents is a SQLite graph library or a recall index.

result.notes: Headline for the owner: this lane is documentation-heavy and measurement-light. Seven weeks of Oct 2026 workflow work produced mechanisms (task.md ownership, hash checkpoints, compact packets, a verify hook, templates) and one tiny real-agent trial in which treatment and baseline were indistinguishable on acceptance (9 of 9 final cases each) and on elapsed time. No tokens, cost or human minutes were ever captured, and eight red-team defects in the gates stayed open. The only recorded byte-saving figure is 10,010 vs 7,947 bytes on constructed fixtures (about 20.6 percent by my division). No SQLite graph library exists in this lane; the nearest items are the optional SQLite measurement index (design only) and the hash-checked compact packet. The untracked context-system line named in AGENTS.md:22 is outside the lane and the likelier match for the owner's memory. The most transferable items for FixFlow are negative controls for gates (RT-01..RT-04 shapes, app check counting skips as failure), early end-to-end proof (effectiveness-review F05), the evaluation arithmetic bounds, and the honest-limits report vocabulary. Caution: the testbed's harness was Codex; Claude Code usage telemetry was never examined.

result.lane: A8 throughput, parallelism and everything else (clinic repo, git history since 2026-11-01, operating documents, owner-recollection hunt, outside folders)

cards.name: Parallel test runner with serial race pass and proof that every test ran once (faster check, USER-22)
cards.what_it_is: scripts/check.py runs the test step as a pytest-xdist parallel pass (6 workers, one PostgreSQL test database per worker, --dist load) plus a single-process pass for tests marked serial (two-connection race tests, timing assertions, random-id tests). It proves from recorded test ids that the two passes ran every test exactly once, and fails on any skip, xfail, xpass, deselect or unrun test. A hung pass is killed by a stall watchdog (CLINIC_CHECK_STALL_SECONDS, default 600). Non-durable Postgres settings (fsync off) in compose.yaml for the test container only. A bounded connect retry for a Windows socket refusal; any retry in the serial pass fails the step.
cards.measured: Whole check 855.2 s (one run; pytest alone 843.3 s) before, 268.3 to 298.3 s over 12 full runs, mean 283.8 s after: about 3.0 times faster (faster-check/task.md:11). 1,953 tests one pass ~850 s -> parallel pass 160-190 s (1,844 tests, 6 workers) + serial pass 104-105 s (128 tests) (task.md:13). Worker sweep on 1,997 tests: 0 workers 746.7 s, 2 -> 443.9, 4 -> 319.6, 6 -> 289.4 to 290.7 (six runs), 8 -> 281.1; eight workers save 9 s (3 percent) over six (task.md:175-185). Non-durable DB: 316 s to 297 s, inside noise, so the check is CPU-bound not flush-bound (task.md:44). Single start-up cost was pytest tmp_path symlink creation, about 32 s on this machine, not the database (task.md:36). Planning brief records before-state: 999 seconds of tests for 1,953 tests while three other checks ran (clinic-planning-brief.md:44). Failure demonstrations A-D: a dying worker under loadfile hung 754 s until the 600 s watchdog, under load it failed in 274 s (task.md:65).
cards.limits: Does not remove the queue between sessions (see A8-02), does not fix the Windows-to-Docker path cost, and the root of the one 600 s hang (B09) is not explained by it: it only bounds such a hang by the watchdog. The race tests stay serial, so the serial pass is now 37 percent of wall time. Timing tests were never run under heavier load than the observed pairs.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Transferable pattern: split tests into a parallel set and a marked-serial set, one DB per worker, and make the runner itself prove from ids that union == plain collect-only list. For pytest-asyncio FastAPI with asyncpg it needs per-worker databases the same way. Measure the real bottleneck first (here a symlink, not CPU or DB). Prefer --dist load over loadfile when a worker can die.

cards.name: Machine-wide check lock with two slots, per-checkout lock, and a memory-headroom gate on the second slot
cards.what_it_is: Evolution of a throttle on concurrent full checks after the PC crashed under load: first a lock directory in the temp folder (one heavy job at a time, board rule), then a file lock held in the repository's common git directory (.git/clinic-check/, shared by every worktree), then slot files (TEST_SLOTS = 2, check.lock and check.lock.1) so two checks may run at once, one check per checkout (second check of the same checkout refused), holder file naming who waits for whom printed once a minute, 45 minute bounded wait, CLINIC_CHECK_NO_LOCK=1 escape that is stated in the summary. Slot 2 opens only while at least 8 GiB of physical memory is available (SECOND_SLOT_FREE_GB = 8.0, GlobalMemoryStatusEx on Windows, MemAvailable on Linux), re-read at every poll. Race tests now decide 'blocked' from pg lock-wait evidence (pg_blocking_pids), not from a 0.6 s elapsed time (FS-01, FS-09, KG-02), because under two checks a slow machine could pass a broken lock.
cards.measured: Five pairs of full checks started together: only pair 1 was two of the author's checks overlapping, 435 s each, against loaded single references 389 to 418 s, i.e. each check 4 to 12 percent slower and about 1.8 to 1.9 times the throughput; on the quiet machine the same code took 275 to 290 s (faster-check/task.md:312-314). Ten checks beside another check passed all tests including race tests (task.md:315). Gate-memory runs after the 8 GiB rule: whole check 1,063.4 s of which 647 s waiting, 405.5 s (3 s wait), 639.7 s (256 s wait), 1,020.4 s (614 s wait); the second slot never opened: in about 980 one-second samples 8 GiB was never available, free memory 2.1 to 4.7 GiB (mean 3.5), 2.4 to 4.6 (3.4), 3.9 to 6.2 (5.2) (task.md:396-406). Minimum free memory with two checks beside six sessions: 0.8, 0.0 and 3.4 GiB (section 14, cited at task.md:406). Board: 'idle sessions and containers left 2 to 6 GiB free, so two checks at once were not measured with the gate' (clinic-build/task.md:778). Root measurement 6 Nov: 0.4 of 24 processors busy while a check waited on the shared lock (clinic-build/task.md:823).
cards.limits: The gate means the second slot is mostly closed, so queue waits of 256 to 647 s persist (B07 stands). The gate reads memory only at admission, not after (Opus P2, task.md:402). Older checkouts on the previous slot code run the two-slot code without the gate. No measurement of two checks beside each other with the gate exists. No diagnosis of why the PC shut down; this is mitigation, not cause (B05). 8 GiB is described as a safety margin, not a measured requirement (task.md:408).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Directly transferable and cheap: put the lock in git rev-parse --git-common-dir so all worktrees share it, use OS file locks (auto-release on kill), show the holder, cap wait time, count slots by memory not by guess, and read available memory (not free) before admitting a second heavy job. Also note the lesson that two concurrent checks make time-based race tests unsound, so base them on lock-wait evidence.

cards.name: Linux container mode of the check (USER-23): tests beside the database
cards.what_it_is: CLINIC_CHECK_MODE=container runs all seven steps in a Debian 12 container (python:3.13-slim-bookworm pinned by digest, locked packages, Playwright Chromium) on the compose network of the checkout's database container, against a hash-verified copy of the working tree (git ls-files cached+others, nothing mounted). 12 workers by default. Container dies with the check (parent-death via stdin pipe, 0.6 s measured), never builds or pulls at check time, never falls back to native. Native mode stays the gate.
cards.measured: Final head df66fc8, 2,246 tests: container mean 117.9 s parallel, 94.0 s serial, 230.1 s whole (three runs 247.0, 215.6, 227.7) against Windows-native 236.1 / 126.5 / 367.2 (and 346.8, 336.8 on earlier heads): about 1.5 times faster as a whole, 34 percent less; parallel pass 1.9 times faster, serial 1.3 times; mypy slower (9.7 s cold vs 1.4 s) (linux-test-runner/task.md:7-18). Container start 6 to 7 s; start plus collect 16 s. Image 2.28 GB; cold build 6 min 28 s (Chromium step 287 s) (task.md:35). Root's earlier diagnosis: Windows-to-published-port round trip 0.63 ms against 0.13 ms inside the container; com.docker.backend port forwarder 0.7 cores; Docker/WSL VM 2.7 cores; six workers 2.45 cores; machine at 42 percent of 24 logical processors (faster-check/task.md:322). The first Linux run found two real Linux-only test failures (commit 19b3906).
cards.limits: Optional; the Windows-native check is still the gate (B06 stands, B18 only partly closed: Linux runs exist but are not the gate). Not verified: a hung test planted inside a container (task.md:69, 164). Inside the container MemAvailable is the host's. Cost is a 2.3 GB image and Docker Hub/Debian/Playwright downloads. Runs still queue behind the same slots. Measured on a machine shared with other sessions, so numbers are loaded, not idle.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Strong transfer: run the gate on the production OS (Linux) in a container next to the DB container rather than through the Windows port forwarder; hash-verify the copied tree; make the container die with the host; refuse silently falling back to another mode. FixFlow (FastAPI+asyncpg tests against Postgres) would gain the same Windows-to-Docker latency saving.

cards.name: Throughput record from git history: commits and merges per day, 3 to 10 November 2026
cards.what_it_is: Count of commits per day on all branches and of first-parent merges onto main, derived by light git log commands. 432 commits total, of which 6 in October (1 to 2 Oct) and 426 since 1 Nov; one commit author identity ('Local workflow implementation', 361 non-merge commits since 1 Nov). Zero commits on 7 and 8 November. Last commit before the halt on 6 November at 14:57, next commit 9 November (first-parent day). Busiest single hours 6 Nov 14:00 (24 commits), 9 Nov 20:00 (18), 6 Nov 12:00 (18).
cards.measured: Per-day commits, all branches: 1 Nov 4, 2 Nov 6, 3 Nov 59, 4 Nov 113, 5 Nov 42, 6 Nov 150, 9 Nov 41, 10 Nov 11 (sum 426). Merge commits by day: 4, 10, 5, 28, 12, 6 for 3,4,5,6,9,10 Nov (sum 65). First-parent merges onto main by day: 3 Nov 4, 4 Nov 8, 5 Nov 5, 6 Nov 8, 9 Nov 5, 10 Nov 6 (sum 36). 7 and 8 Nov: no commits. Slices merged: S01-S03 on 3 Nov, S04-S08 on 4 Nov, S09-S10 on 5 Nov.
cards.limits: Commit counts are not a quality or efficiency measure (many commits are record, review-fix and merge-main commits; B01 fix rounds inflate them). No token, cost or wall-clock-per-slice figure exists in the repository for these days. The halt gap is visible but the cause (usage limit) comes from the board, not from git.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A cheap, reproducible throughput baseline (commits and first-parent merges per day, plus gap days) that FixFlow can compute with two git commands before and after any harness change; pair it with per-slice token counts, which the clinic repository never recorded.

cards.name: Orchestration rules: model tiers, session tree depth 3, fan-out of 3, state in the repository
cards.what_it_is: docs/agentic-coding/orchestration.md (adopted 2 Nov 2026): root session (Fable) holds the wave board, writes briefs, reads every diff, judges gates and merges; slice leads Opus-high for money/stock/migration/permission slices, Sonnet with Opus reviewer for mechanical ones; Haiku/Sonnet/Opus subagent roles; model and effort passed explicitly on every start; depth root, slice, one child level, subagents; at most three running children per node; every node owns one file set, worktree, branch and port-distinct database; merges flow upward; shared documents edited only by the root; state in docs/tasks/<id>/task.md so a dead session is resumed from branch plus task record; brief contract block; cost rules (deterministic work inline before any agent, discovery agents return facts not verdicts, Opus skeptics only where a gate could change, hard cap with an open-risks list).
cards.measured: none for the rules themselves (no cost or time comparison with another structure). Observed outcome: 12 slices and about 20 follow-up branches merged in 8 days (see A8-04). Stated rationale numbers: a parent sees a 400-character note per turn per session level; three levels is where 'the loss is still cheaper than doing the work serially' (orchestration.md:18) - asserted, not measured.
cards.limits: The root is a serial gate (B04): the board reached 219,111 bytes and over 800 lines and the root's context overflowed. Shared-document single-writer rule creates B13. Subagent file writes refused so reports return through the orchestrator's context (orchestration.md:14, B16). No rule fixes the new defects introduced by fix rounds (B01). The 'start sessions without asking' (USER-21) was blocked by the app: a start is accepted only on a turn the owner's message began (clinic-build/task.md:823, 825).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Reusable as a template the owner already built from FixFlow's own design (orchestration.md:79 says it adapts the FixFlow tier guide and script contract). Transferable parts: explicit model/effort per start, one file set per node, task.md as the resume point, root-only shared documents, brief contract. Parts to improve for FixFlow: move the board off one 219 KB file, and let children write their own proposed shared-doc edits to a machine-appliable patch to cut B13.

cards.name: Usage-limit halt of 6 November and manual resume, plus the owner-turn start constraint
cards.what_it_is: A usage limit stopped every session on 6 Nov at about 14:57; nothing was lost (main clean at f2390bd, every branch with commits or uncommitted work). On 9 Nov the root restarted Docker Desktop and the nine databases in use and resumed the sessions. Separately, the app accepted a new session start only on a turn that the owner's message began, so follow-up sessions were created on the owner's turn and waited as cards for the root's go; the owner's leave-running instruction was recorded as USER-21 reaffirmed. The Codex context-system harness has a --continue flag for a usage limit, but that harness was not wired to the clinic sessions.
cards.measured: Gap: no commits between 6 Nov 14:57 and the 9 Nov restart (git log; see A8-04 table, 7 and 8 Nov zero). Orchestration.md:20 notes the account session limit is shared by every running session and 'the notebook reconciliation hit it once'. No figure for token use per session or per slice was recorded.
cards.limits: Nothing in the repository automates resume, Docker/container start, or session creation without an owner message. Recovery depended on state living in git and task records, which worked (no work lost). No scheduler, cron or unattended-run mechanism exists in the repository.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Transfer the part that worked: durable state in the repository (branch plus task.md) so a halt loses nothing. The unsolved part (unattended start, usage-aware pacing, restarting Docker and DB containers after reboot) needs new work; the repository provides no design for it.

cards.name: Two unclean PC shutdowns and the load rules that followed
cards.what_it_is: After two unclean shutdowns of the PC under concurrent full test runs (5 and 6 Nov), the root limited work to three or four children at once and one full check at a time, enforced by a lock directory clinic-full-check.lock in the user's temp folder, until all worktrees merged the git-directory lock (FC-10). On 6 Nov the owner asked for the machine to be used (USER-23) and the rule 'one heavy job at a time' was retired in favour of slots (A8-02), VM drills allowed beside checks. The staging VM's NAT range changed at a PC reboot and locked ssh out (commit 855acaa).
cards.measured: The cause was not diagnosed; no crash dump, event log or memory trace is cited. Observation after mitigation: free memory 0.0 to 0.8 GiB at lows with two checks beside six sessions, 2 to 6 GiB with one (faster-check/task.md:406). Free memory 10.8 of 31 GB during a single check beside a VM drill (task.md:322).
cards.limits: Memory pressure is inferred, not shown; a hardware or driver cause is not excluded. Mitigation reduces concurrency (and so throughput) instead of reducing per-session memory. Idle sessions and database containers (nine databases in use at restart; B08 says 26 containers) are not addressed by any mechanism in the repository.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Do not assume the cause. Transferable: sample whole-machine CPU and free memory once a second during parallel work (the repo's sampler wrote run-N-system.csv; note its free_mb column contains a thousands comma, so naive CSV reads give 3 instead of 3,523), and set concurrency from measured available memory, not core count.

cards.name: Per-checkout isolation: own worktree, branch, port, test database, lock
cards.what_it_is: Each slice session works in its own git worktree (.claude/worktrees/<name>) on its own branch with its own compose project, database container port (e.g. 55440, 55455, 55460) and database names suffixed with a hash of the checkout path (test_<name>_<hash>_gw<N>); the container mode passes an explicit checkout tag. Migration numbering rule: one writer at a time per app; the second branch regenerates its migration after merge. Shared documents are read-only for slices. 19 worktrees exist under .claude/worktrees.
cards.measured: none (no collision count). Recorded failures: two runs of one checkout at once dropped each other's test database, 115 errors (faster-check/task.md:392); older branches still locked a per-user file, so the two lock generations did not exclude each other (FC-10, clinic-build/task.md:823).
cards.limits: Each checkout needs its own database container: this is the memory and pile-up cost in B08 and B15 (nine to 26 containers). No mechanism removes finished worktrees, containers or volumes; the root archives nothing without the owner's word (clinic-build/task.md:821).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Transferable: per-worktree compose project plus port, path-hash in database names so checkouts cannot touch each other, and a rule that a second check of the same checkout is refused. To address B08, consider one shared database container with per-checkout databases instead of one container per worktree (the clinic repo did this per checkout, and the check paid memory for it).

cards.name: Gate discipline: root verification, adversarial Opus review and the fix-round record
cards.what_it_is: Every slice branch passes a root gate: the root reads the diff and the task record, runs the check on the merged main, requires one or more Opus reviewers 'briefed to refute', then re-reviews fixes; defects get ids (G05-01, KF-01, FS-01...), severity P1/P2/P3, owner and closing commit on the wave board. Fix rounds are numbered (round 1, 2, 3 and the 'gate round 6' of the faster check). Records state what a reviewer could not check (for example the Opus round 6 found the author's own commit failed mypy, a P1, because the author ran ruff and tests but not mypy).
cards.measured: Counts quoted per branch, for example faster check: one P1 of the author's own at round 6, P3s listed; S11 gate round 2 returned GT-01 to GT-27 including two record claims the cited evidence did not support (a large-volume restore replaced by a small one, a log-secret scan with nine needles while the record said 55) (clinic-build/task.md:660); kernel follow-up: KF-01 to KF-11, no P1 (task.md:~765). Merge-gate checks on main: 1997 tests in 286 s, 2106 in 322 s, 2173 in 329 s, 2304 in 420 s, 2406 in 387 s, 2520 tests (7/7) at the end.
cards.limits: It is model reading code (B17): no independent human review; reports overstate (B12 confirmed by the GT round); fixes introduced new defects (B01; the board shows one slice needing rounds 1 to 3 and the faster check 6). The first-round Opus refute-review mostly returned P2/P3, with no measurement of what fraction of defects each round found or introduced.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Transferable: reviewers briefed to refute with a numbered defect ledger; the rule that records must state what evidence cannot show (the GT finding). Gap to fill: a deterministic claims-vs-evidence check (does the cited test exist, does the cited number appear in the cited log) to cut B12, which the repository did not build.

cards.name: Check runner design: controlled environment, failure demonstrations and 'nothing weaker' proofs
cards.what_it_is: scripts/check.py is the only gate: ruff lint, ruff format, mypy strict, Django checks, missing migrations, DB probe, pytest. The child environment drops PYTHON*, PYTEST_*, DJANGO_* variables, plugin autoload off, settings fixed to clinic.settings.test; any skip, xfail, xpass or deselect fails; tests start inside a Windows job object (parent-death signal on Linux) so killing the check kills pytest and workers; SIGTERM/SIGHUP/Ctrl-Break stop it cleanly. Each change to the check was shown by planted failures (failing test, erroring fixture, skip, xfail, serial failure, a dying worker, a hung test, a six-fault file) that the check had to fail on. This is the nearest thing in the repository to a verification harness that is itself tested.
cards.measured: S00: exit 0, 7/7, 220 tests, 0 skipped; fails as intended on an added skip, an added tests.py, a stopped database; ignores an injected PYTEST_ADDOPTS, PYTEST_PLUGINS, DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and PYTHONPATH (s00-baseline/task.md:53-55). The root's demonstration on main with a file of six planted faults: 3,017 files copied and verified by hash, CHECK FAILED 5/7, collected=2526 passed=2520 failed=2 errors=2 skipped=1 xfailed=1 (clinic-build/task.md:796).
cards.limits: Checks the code, not a clean install end to end (B02: nobody walked a fresh install). The check ran against a synthetic seeder only. A real Android-style native compile or real host run is not in scope (B19).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Highly transferable: an unforgeable gate (cannot pass on skipped or unrun tests, cannot be steered by environment), a tested watchdog, and process-tree kill. FixFlow's CI could adopt the id-union proof and the planted-fault demonstrations.

cards.name: Query follow-up and load drill rerun (page speed) with the 12-clerk load not rerun
cards.what_it_is: Drill j on the staging VM rig: money and overview pages at about 75,000 documents, before and after set-based queries (the query follow-up, merged 10 Nov). Earlier load drills e (contention, 24 synthetic clerks, 5 minutes, locust, GUNICORN_WORKERS=8) failed, with aggregated percentile figures up to 110,000 ms.
cards.measured: After the query follow-up: money and overview pages answer in 0.1 to 0.5 s at 75,016 documents (9 to 13 s before) (commit f2e6ec5; board line 821). The 12-clerk load on the new code was not rerun (clinic-build/task.md:821). Drill e: locust exit status 1 after 301 s, aggregated 99th-percentile-class columns of 11,000 to 110,000 ms with 809 requests (e_load_contention md, FAIL line and the Aggregated row).
cards.limits: The 12 concurrent users claim is untested after the fix (B20). The rig is a local Hyper-V VM, not a real host (B19).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Pattern only: a scripted staging VM with timed drills and committed raw evidence; run the same drill before and after a fix and record both numbers, which this record did for page time but not for concurrency.

cards.name: Context system for long Claude Code sessions (compaction hooks, state restore, exact local recall)
cards.what_it_is: tools/context_system: Python standard-library hooks. Setting autoCompactWindow 400000 (compaction near 367k tokens); PreCompact hook snapshots declared task-state sections (restore markers, whole small file, or named sections like Next action / Decisions / Ruled out) plus a factual ledger and raw window copy; SessionStart(compact) restores the snapshot verbatim and reports sections changed on disk; one reminder per cycle about 40k tokens early; a file over 30 KB returns its first page and an outline; ctx.py recall search/show finds exact earlier text in main and subagent transcripts and the archive by lexical regex over transcript files, no model calls, no database. tools/context_system_codex is the Codex adaptation (7 project-local hooks, immutable checksummed snapshots, journal recall bounded to 2,048 bytes per response). Both stay untracked in git and are on no clinic route; AGENTS.md says they are to move to their own repository.
cards.measured: Claude system: 85 regression tests; 'not installed in this project and not yet run in a live session'; quality at 300-400k 'unmeasured until the comparison in eval/ has been run' (tools/context_system/README.md:3). Local overhead measured offline on 2026-10-10 (three-project-deck/A-research/SLM-LOCAL/evidence.md:20): hook run time 0.1-0.2 s; recall search over all 211 of this project's real transcripts (115.3 MB) 0.52-1.06 s at 22-31 MB peak working set across six query types; PreCompact on copies 0.11-0.15 s at 61-69 MB peak. Codex comparison 15 Oct (RESULTS_2026-10-15.md): native, maintained notes and adapter all 15/15 recall and 100% task; ordinary input 720,036 / 794,310 / 842,620 (adapter 6.08 percent above maintained notes, 17.02 percent above native); first resumed boundary 4,962 bytes exceeded the 4 KiB aggregate gate; 'no improvement from the adapter or from maintained notes over native Codex'. 12 Oct pilot: adapter used 10.31 percent more ordinary reported input (codex README:11). 14 Oct screen: all arms hit caps unfinished, partial scores 76.19, 76.19, 71.43; no arm used journal recall (SLM-LOCAL evidence.md:58). Before fixes the hooks had 53 defects over four review rounds, including 15 of 48 restored sections lost to a character cap (evidence.md:18-19).
cards.limits: This is the closest thing to 'faster recall that minimises token use' in the repository, but it is lexical text recall over transcripts, not a graph and not SQLite; it recalls only what was said in a session, not the repository's structure. No comparison showed a token or quality gain; the only measured token result is a cost increase. It is untracked, never installed in the clinic sessions, so it did not affect the clinic build. Claude version-specific hooks depend on an undocumented PreCompact behaviour (README).
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Transferable design points: restore only declared task-state blocks whole-or-nothing, keep a small hard byte budget, make recall exact and paged with integrity hashes, and measure before claiming a gain. Do not assume a token saving: the repository's own measured result is none. Hook code for Claude Code could be lifted for FixFlow, but needs a live A/B first (eval/ harness exists, dry run only).

cards.name: Corpus map: persisted typed-edge map of the planning documents with coverage ledger (closest to a graph library)
cards.what_it_is: output/corpus-map-justification: a method to persist a 'map of the plan as written' (dependencies, derivations, intermediate reasoning steps, exact source spans, unresolved references, read/linked/unresolved coverage) and serve bounded evidence-carrying context packets to fresh agents. 09-operational/tools/cmap.py stores it as JSONL files (s1.jsonl attested edges, s2 vocabulary, s3 identity, s4 gap annotations, candidates.jsonl, chunks.jsonl, ledger.json), computes packets from base records on every call, with a pinned Graphify 0.9.81 comparator built to graph.json (92 nodes, 127 edges, 10 communities). Run 6 to 7 Oct under a constraint block: 8 lanes, one reasoner, one skeptic.
cards.measured: Justification pass: one design with 99 rules, 55 borrowed from verified quotes and 44 'required: no source covers it'; skeptic 21 attacks, 12 accepted and 9 rejected (06-final/report.md). The pilot check 'did not reproduce the independent annotator's chain at any level' and reproduced the frozen gap only partly (06-final/report.md). Operational phase state: Graphify graph.json built (92 nodes, 127 edges); fresh-agent trials 'not started' (P9-5) and verdict 'not started' (P9-9) (SESSION_STATE.md:54-59). No token or time measurement of delivered context.
cards.limits: Storage is JSONL, not SQLite; there is no networkx or SQL graph. It targets planning-document markdown, not code; no live comparison of delivered context against routed reading was finished. Stopped at P9-4 (the repository records no verdict). Untracked, to be moved with the context-system line.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Idea-free fact: the method's separation of attested records, decisions, candidate similarities and a coverage ledger (read/linked/unresolved) is a worked design for a persisted knowledge map with explicit gaps. A FixFlow version would face the same unfinished validation; reuse the store layout and the 'recompute packets from base records' rule, not a conclusion.

cards.name: Doc-context small language model for evolving documentation (proposed, nothing run)
cards.what_it_is: Experiment design for a local small model with two tasks: T-A, produce a bounded doc-state projection (target 4,096 bytes for Codex; about 9,000 characters for Claude Code) from the current docs, the diff since the last projection and the task, with a source pointer on every statement; T-B, flag stale summaries by source hash (not by model judgement) and draft edits. Part of a 'three-project deck' whose third project is an SLM for 'evolving-documentation context management'. Evidence file concludes no measured retrieval bottleneck justifies a GPU summarizer.
cards.measured: Premises only: the real task-state file was 17,174 characters at hand-off against a 9,000-character budget (n=1); docs about 1.36 MB, estimated 339k to 521k tokens (experiment-design.md:12 premises, citing SLM-LOCAL-r1-27 and PR-LOCAL-r1-24). The design states 'Nothing in this document has been run'. Evidence line r1-26: none of the local records measures a selection or retrieval bottleneck (evidence.md:36).
cards.limits: Designed only; privacy rule keeps clinic files out of every dataset. A different project from the clinic application and an adjunct to the workflow research. The idea of detecting staleness by source hash rather than model judgement is the part that is cheap and testable.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The most reusable fact: stale-summary detection by source hash is deterministic and cheap, so shared documents (B13, board and AGENTS.md drift) could be refreshed or flagged by a script before any model is involved. The SLM itself is unmeasured.

cards.name: Scheduler-system (Pulse) knowledge graph: Graphiti on Neo4j, a different project
cards.what_it_is: C:\Bilal_Migration\...\28_Misc_Ideas\scheduler-system--main is a scheduling assistant (Task 1 NLP extraction, Task 2 schedule generation, Task 3 Graphiti storage) whose pulse_kg_schema.md v4 defines entity types User, Task, Event with learned scheduling preferences and temporal bi-fact edges. graphiti_client/ writes structured JSON episodes to Neo4j (NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD in client.py:24-35), bypassing Graphiti's LLM extraction to fix a CypherTypeError (docs/architecture.md:1-3). It models a user's schedule preferences, not a repository.
cards.measured: none read (README-level look only; no benchmark found in the files named)
cards.limits: Graph database is Neo4j via Graphiti, not SQLite. A temporal knowledge graph over personal scheduling data is the likeliest other source of the owner's 'graph-based' memory, but it is a scheduler product, not a self-evolving repository and not a recall layer for code sessions.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Only as a pattern reference: structured JSON episodes written straight to a temporal graph store avoid LLM extraction at write time. Nothing in it addresses development speed or token cost.

cards.name: Subagent file-write refusal and the 400-character handoff
cards.what_it_is: Orchestration rules state that subagents reply with their full result as text and that file writes from subagents are refused in this environment, so long reports pass through the orchestrator's context; a parent session sees a 400-character note per turn from a child and must read the diff itself. Mitigations in the rules: batch claims per verifier, tiny tasks inline, Haiku for typed-schema extraction, children keep their own task.md and evidence folders.
cards.measured: none
cards.limits: Nothing in the repository works around the refusal; the 400-character figure is a stated property of the harness, not measured here. The Codex workflow run (Codex/2026-10-31/run-sol-6-1-subagents-with) had subagents write research notes into a work folder instead, a different environment.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Design for the constraint: have subagents return typed, compact schemas (the clinic root already asks discovery agents for facts, lines and names, never verdicts), and put heavy evidence in files written by a session that can write.

cards.name: Human/agent presentation split and agent context routing (lean workflow reassessment)
cards.what_it_is: Decision of 5 Oct 2026: keep a separate human view (docs/human/README.md with diagrams, choices, status vocabulary) and compact task-specific agent packets; reject blanket documentation bans and replacement of shared state with private memory; routing by a context map (docs/agentic-coding/project-context-routing.md) and the AGENTS.md routing section. The root AGENTS.md was 28 lines and 6,709 bytes at baseline. Measurement of any productivity or token saving is declared absent.
cards.measured: 'We have no demonstrated local productivity or token-saving multiplier' (docs/human/README.md:34). AGENTS.md is 10,698 bytes now (file size). The context map still names old A/Q/T ranges (clinic-build/task.md:36).
cards.limits: Documents drift (B13): parts of AGENTS.md and the context map are stale. The routing is a reading convention, not enforced access exclusion (human/README.md:24). No measurement.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The compact-task-packet plus human-view split transfers; so does the lesson that routing documents rot without a hash or CI check tying them to the code.

cards.name: Staleness and 'what was not measured' habit: honest status labels
cards.what_it_is: Records label every fact VERIFIED-BY-COMMAND, VERIFIED-IN-CODE, INFERRED, and the project documents distinguish REPORTED/OBSERVED/DOCUMENTED/INFERRED/PROPOSED/UNKNOWN. Examples inside the throughput record: FS-08 states that the gate 'was not measured', the memory figure of 8 GiB is 'a safety margin, not a measured requirement', the container hung-test case is 'not verified'. The root, by contrast, finds sessions' reports overstate (GT round).
cards.measured: none
cards.limits: Labels are written by the same model that produced the claim; B12 shows they were wrong at least twice (a replaced restore run, a needle count 9 against 55). No automated link from a label to an artifact.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: Adopt the label vocabulary but add a machine check that every VERIFIED-BY-COMMAND label links to a saved log under evidence/ that exists and contains the quoted number.

cards.name: Owner-recollection test: SQLite graph library and faster recall
cards.what_it_is: Search result, stated plainly: the clinic repository holds no SQLite graph library for a self-evolving repository. The only .sqlite/.db-style hits are (a) a vendored hook file output/corpus-map-justification/10-context-admission-research/sources/claude-context-hooks/hooks/lib/cairn_graph_footer.py (a third-party cch/cairn tool using sqlite3, a callers/tests footer on code reads) and its test, (b) a test about Django migration graphs, and (c) FACTS in eval_live.py naming SQLite as a rejected database. Closest actual matches: A8-12 (exact lexical recall plus compaction snapshot hooks, minimising token loss but unmeasured as a saving), A8-13 (JSONL typed-edge corpus map with coverage ledger, unfinished), A8-14 (doc-context SLM and hash staleness, designed only), research notes on external systems that do use SQLite graph or memory stores (Virtual Context: canonical originals in SQLite/Postgres; LCM 0.16.0: raw SQLite history and summary DAG; MemTree in Claude Code Infinite) in output/context-system-research/report.md, all researched not built here; and the separate Pulse Graphiti/Neo4j graph (A8-15). So the owner's memory is plausibly a blend of the research on external systems and the corpus map, not an artifact built here.
cards.measured: Report states the closest shipped match is Claude Code Infinite 1.0.14 with MemTree (hosted), maintainer-reported: MemTree 68.7/100 at 39M total input per run, full-history 69.3/100 at 113M, native compact 48.7/100 at 17M; compression from about 775k to about 420k; that is a third-party small benchmark, three runs, not reproduced here (output/context-system-research/report.md:21-27). Distil's own pilot: 4.5 percent smaller prompts per step and 9.7 percent more cost on six tasks; Parsec vendor test: 62 versus 57 solved, mean peak context about 41k versus 80k (report.md table). The research installed nothing and used no memory service (README.md last paragraph).
cards.limits: Third-party numbers only; the clinic repository did not install or run any of these. The research is explicitly not adoption. Nothing from it was used by the clinic sessions.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: The research files are a ready comparison of MemTree, Virtual Context, YesMem, LCM, Rolling Context, Distil, Parsec, Jev/Scalpel to build on, with pins and source links; FixFlow should treat all numbers as vendor-reported and run its own A/B using the tools/context_system/eval harness.

cards.name: Archiving and progress-visibility rules: what the repository says
cards.what_it_is: The root archives nothing without the owner's word (board paragraph of 10 Nov, 6 Nov: 'It archives nothing'); the board keeps a per-slice row with session, tier, branch, worktree and port; each session keeps docs/tasks/<id>/task.md with status, current state and next action; the root reads the diff and not the turn note. Progress visibility to the owner is the board and the human README; no live status mechanism (dashboard, notification) is described in the repository files read.
cards.measured: none. The board file is 219,111 bytes (wc -c); the owner's B14 (a step display not moving for an hour) is not described in any file read.
cards.limits: No mechanism for pruning idle sessions, worktrees (19 under .claude/worktrees), containers or old databases is found. The owner pays attention through one large board file that the root edits alone.
cards.transfer_to_fixflow: A per-session row (branch, worktree, port, tier, status) is cheap and portable; add an automatic expiry list (worktrees with merged branches, containers without a live checkout) and a short progress file written by each session every N minutes so progress is visible without reading the board.

result.notes: Plain answer to the owner's recollection: no SQLite graph library, no .sqlite or .db file, and no networkx exist in the clinic repository. What exists that could be remembered as it: (1) tools/context_system, a built-but-never-installed compaction and exact lexical-recall hook set (A8-12) whose only measured token result is a cost increase (adapter 6.08 percent above maintained notes, 17.02 percent above native, tools/context_system_codex/RESULTS_2026-10-15.md); (2) the corpus map, a JSONL typed-edge store with a coverage ledger, validation unfinished (A8-13); (3) a doc-context small-language-model design, designed only, with hash-based stale detection (A8-14); (4) a research report on external memory systems that use SQLite (Virtual Context, LCM) and hosted memory trees (MemTree), none adopted (A8-19); (5) the unrelated Pulse scheduler's Graphiti/Neo4j knowledge graph (A8-15). All context-system material is untracked in git and is slated to move to its own repository per AGENTS.md. The hard, measured throughput gains actually delivered in this repository are in the check: 855.2 s to about 284 s (parallel runner), a further 34 percent via container mode on Linux (230.1 s vs 350 s mean), two slots with a memory gate, and the id-union proof; these address B06, B07, B09 and B18 but leave B03, B05 (cause), B08, B10, B14, B16 and B20 mostly unsolved. Commit throughput per day is in the data table (426 commits, 65 merges since 1 Nov; 36 first-parent merges on main; none on 7 and 8 Nov). Counts of commits per day on first-parent main use the `git log main --first-parent` command and the merge count 65 includes merges of main into branches. The 'Local workflow implementation' author name covers 361 non-merge commits, so authorship cannot be used to separate sessions. Note: the 4 Nov line in the clinic planning brief says USER-21 'at most three running children' while the board line 823 says three or four after the shutdowns; both are quoted as recorded.

missed_cards.name: Root orchestrator's auto-memory: agent-written lesson store (feedback memories with Why / How to apply)
missed_cards.what_it_is: Outside the repository, the clinic root session keeps 15 memory files under C:\Users\User\.claude\projects\C--Bilal-Migration-User-Downloads-20-PROJECTS-24-Clinic-Workshop\memory (MEMORY.md index plus one file per lesson, each with frontmatter, a Why line and a How-to-apply line, cross-linked with [[...]]). The lessons were written by the agent after failures or owner corrections and are loaded into every later root session. Examples: tiered-model-orchestration.md (always pass model and effort; an omitted model inherited Fable at max and an S00 session had to be restarted; never run the root's check in a slice worktree while that session runs its own, because the shared test DB name collides with 'database is being accessed by other users'; root edits to the docs break doc-reading tests, so expect one fix-up round); use-the-machine-parallelism.md (measure before serialising; batch several ready branches into one check on the merged tree; a step display that does not move is no evidence of a stall, so check branch commit times and processes); shared-temp-clobbers-logs.md; subagents-return-text-not-files.md; bash-cr-check-lies.md; python-write-crlf-on-windows.md; hyperv-rig-gotchas.md; clinic-folder-bloat-audit-2026-11.md. An older OneDrive-slug memory folder holds pro-plan-workflow-limits.md and summarize-before-executing.md.
missed_cards.measured: Size: 15 files, 81,266 bytes in total by wc -c (one file, clinic-s00-readiness-2026-11.md, is 50,136 bytes). Costs recorded inside it: the bloat audit 'cost 18 agents and 1.5M tokens' (clinic-folder-bloat-audit-2026-11.md:19); a 16-minute check had to be rerun because another session's log replaced it in $TEMP (shared-temp-clobbers-logs.md:11); each Hyper-V trap 'cost 10-40 minutes of blind retries' (hyperv-rig-gotchas.md:19). Root measurement of 6 Nov: 0.4 of 24 processors busy, 0.63 ms vs 0.13 ms round trip (use-the-machine-parallelism.md:13). Nobody measured whether the memory reduces repeated mistakes.
missed_cards.limits: Machine-local and per project slug: worktree sessions (18 slugs) have their own folders, and nothing ties the folders together. Not in git (B11). The index is loaded whole on every start (the PR-LOCAL lane counts memory files among the fixed overhead). Nothing promotes a lesson into the repository's conventions or checks automatically. Gaps neither repository closes: promote durable lessons into CLAUDE.md or a test, give each lesson a check date, and share lessons across worktree slugs.

missed_cards.name: Parked-start technique: pre-create dependent sessions on the owner's turn, release them later with SendMessage
missed_cards.what_it_is: The app refuses start_session ('user_asked') on any turn that an automated event (a session note or a background task) began, even with the standing authorisation USER-21 recorded. The root's workaround on 6 Nov: on the owner's own turn, pre-create the follow-up sessions with a brief that opens 'PARKED START: reply one line and end your turn; begin only on the root's go'. When a dependency merges, release each one with SendMessage ('go: merge main at <commit> first'), because SendMessage works on automated turns and starts do not. When a start is refused, propose an 'own_initiative' card with the full brief, and batch cards so that one word from the owner starts several.
missed_cards.measured: none. Used on 6 Nov for three parked sessions: kernel-followup (port 55452), people-followup (55453) and posting-followups (55454), all waiting on the opening cutoff guards merge (clinic-build-standing-start-authorization.md:17).
